articles.title: Why Utah nabbed undersized DT Jireh Moe from the transfer portal when other teams ‘shied away’
articles.summary: A lot of teams ‘shied away’ from ‘undersized’ DT Jireh Moe in transfer portal. Utah didn’t, and now Moe is breaking out in a young Ute defensive tackles room...
articles.body:
On paper, Jireh Moe doesn't look like your prototypical college football defensive tackle.

Moe is officially listed on Utah's roster at 6-foot, though head coach Morgan Scalley admits that he's actually shorter than that, and at 280 pounds, he's a good 20-plus pounds lighter than most of his teammates in his position room.

Moe's measurables, along with the fact that he previously played at bottom-dwelling Group of Six school San Jose State , perhaps caused some coaches to skip over him when he entered the transfer portal after the 2025 season.

Scalley and his coaching staff, however, turned on the tape and liked what they saw.

Moe's one-on-one reps against Power Four competition especially stood out to Scalley and the Utes' recruiting team, leading them to believe he would be able to excel when facing that level of team nearly every week while at Utah.

In fact, Scalley said the Utes' analytics showed that Moe was one of the best defensive tackles available in the transfer portal. 247Sports ranked him as the No. 97 defensive lineman in the 2026 portal, while On3 had him as the No. 293 defensive lineman.

Utah's staff seeing something not many other people did has been a hallmark of Scalley's going back to his time recruiting underrated defensive players such as Devin Lloyd , a two-star prospect in high school who is now one of the NFL's best linebackers.

With Moe, the measureables didn't matter nearly as much as the talent that was evident while he was at San Jose State.

"What we saw on film is he's a football player," Scalley said. "He's a football player and you saw him going up against really good competition, and again, you always look for those one-on-one matchups. When they're in a one-on-one situation, are they winning?

"Our analytics said that he was the best in the pool of anyone, but people, because of his size, a lot of people shied away from him. We did not, because again, he showed it versus powerful teams. I don't know of many that have a better personality."

Moe never started in his freshman season at San Jose State in 2025, but quickly grew into a dependable rotation option. He gained the trust of the coaching staff, making his debut at No. 6 Texas , where he graded out as one of the Spartans' best defensive players in the game after registering two tackles and a quarterback hurry.

Against Stanford , Moe was once against one of the best defenders for San Jose State. Those two games, plus a season stat line of 28 tackles, two tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks and a team-high PFF season grade of 83.1 suggested that Moe was ready to make the leap to the next level of college football.

All offseason long, Ute coaches talked up Moe, with defensive tackles coach Luther Elliss saying during fall camp that Moe has been one of the most consistent players since spring ball.

"He understands that he has to be a technician, and he's very good, if not one of our best technicians day in and day out, so I think that really helps him," Elliss said. "He is strong and explosive. He's very explosive and he has some really good things."

While Moe has to be more of a technician than some other defensive tackles who can overwhelm offensive linemen with their size, developing that deep skill set has been what has allowed him to rise to the top of Utah's depth chart.

And a certain height and size isn't required to be great, as Ellliss, who played 10 seasons at defensive tackle in the NFL, reminds us.

"Just start looking at John Randle, Warren Sapp, Aaron Donald . You look at all those guys, some of the greatest ones here recently are around that six-foot mark, 280-ish, 300 maybe," Elliss said.

"To me, size, the measureables are what they are — measureables. At the end of the day, it's about can you play this game, and (Moe) can play this game."

Though he started in the Utes' season-opener against Idaho , Moe played just 14 snaps and did not register a tackle. Ute coaches opted to save him for the bigger game against Arkansas and test out some of the depth players at defensive tackle.

Moe was rested and ready to go against Arkansas and turned in a dominant performance.

He was graded Utah's best-performing defensive player with a PFF grade of 85.7 and notched a sack, a team-high two tackles for loss and a quarterback hurry to go alongside eight tackles.

"Jireh Moe, eight tackles, two TFLs, one sack — all over the place," Scalley said. "He didn't show up on the stat sheet Game 1. Sometimes that happens, but the biggest reason we took that guy in the portal was because of the one-on-one matchups that he would consistently win, and that guy is so active. Impressive game from him tonight."

Moe's most impressive play of the game was on his sack of Arkansas quarterback KJ Jackson as he unleashed a spin move to easily get by Razorback offensive lineman Kobe Branham and stick Jackson.

"Just playing fast and just trusting my coaches too on play calls and all that, just putting us in the right spot," Moe said.

Though there's still a long way to go in the 2026 season, Saturday's performance by Moe and fellow starter Karson Kaufusi answered some of the preseason questions surrounding the Utes' young defensive tackles group.

The Utes held Razorbacks to just 2.2 yards per rush and made life difficult for Jackson throughout the game, sacking him four times, forcing seven quarterback hurries and batting passes down at the line of scrimmage.

"Me and Kars, I'm blessed to have him on my side," Moe said. "Kars, he's a very lengthy guy. He's a technician, too. He's a really good player, a really smart player, too. He helped me be who I am today too, technique-wise and getting smarter and getting in my playbook, but I believe we complement each other."

While Utah's defensive line will face greater challenges than a below-standard Arkansas offensive line this season, the Hogs still had a lot of size, and the Utes aced its first test.

"If you look at any SEC team that you go against, it's impressive size. At our press conference on Monday, I said, the tale of tape's going to be the offensive line, defensive line and I was so proud of them," Scalley said.

articles.title: Thoughts on a 7-6 Rangers win
articles.summary: Rangers 7, D-Backs 6
articles.body:
And the Rangers win their first road series since June 29-July 1 in Cleveland !

That was also a little more exciting that I'd have preferred.

It did feel like from the outset that the Rangers were going to have success in this game. A line drive single by Justin Foscue to start things off, followed the second-longest home run of Corey Seager 's career, will do that.

Statcast had the Seager homer at 458 feet. Only once in his career — back in 2021, with the Dodgers — has Seager hit the ball farther.

Its also tied with Bryce Eldridge for the 28th longest home run hit this season in the majors.

Its the third longest home run hit at Chase Field this season.

Its the longest home run hit by a Ranger this year. Jake Burger 's 447 foot shot against the Tigers on July 5 was the previous high.

Gabriel Moreno homered off of Cal Quantrill to lead off the fourth, making it a 2-1 game, but then the Rangers capitalized on clownball in the top of the fifth to make it a comfy game.

Justin Foscue reached on an E5 by Nolan Arenado , on a ball that took a bad hope. A line drive Corey Seager single was followed by a Josh Jung single that Lars Nootbar…well…

If you don't want to watch the video, Jung looped it into left field, where Nootbar was coming in for it. He pulled up, realizing in couldn't make the catch, but then had the ball bounce between his legs and behind him, allowing both Foscue and Seager to score. Brandon Nimmo later blooped a two out single into no man's land to bring home Jung, and Texas was up 5-1.

Two more came across the next inning, with Danny Jansen doubling home Ezequiel Duran , Evan Carter pinch hitting for Foscue and smoking it but right at Jordan Lawlar in center, then Seager drilling a single to bring home Jansen.

Seager even advanced to second on the throw, leading Dave Raymond and Mike Bascik to comment on how good, physically, Seager is feeling. Feeling good Corey Seager is a good thing.

Because I'm feeling good about this game and this win, we will not talk about the relievers, other than to note that Robert Garcia did good work in the eighth in the second of back-to-back outings, a good sign, given both how long he was on the injured list as well as how badly the Rangers need quality relief options right now.

Quantrill had thrown just 65 pitches through six, and there seemed to be some question as to whether he'd come back out for the seventh, despite the low pitch count. Quantrill did come out, though he was pulled after allowing a Geraldo Perdomo single.

Post-game, it was reported Quantrill was dealing with back tightness, which is why he didn't go longer.

Meanwhile, the Astros of Houston lost, putting the Rangers two games back in the American League West, though really three, since the Astros have the tiebreaker. The Guardians won, meaning the Rangers are two back in the Wild Card, and the Blue Jays won, which means the Jays are still a game ahead of Texas among the teams chasing the Guardians. Fortunately, Texas has the tiebreaker advantage against both Cleveland and Toronto .

Toronto, I will note, plays three games in Arlington Friday through Sunday, with Cleveland no doubt hoping neither team splits.

Before Toronto is Boston . On the plus side, the Rangers are facing Boston at the Shed. On the minus side, Boston is 82-68 this season, with the third best record in the American League. On the plus side, they are eight and a half back in the division, four and a half back for the first Wild Card spot, and six games up on Cleveland for the third Wild Card spot, so while they are not going to be treating the games like exhibitions, their postseason berth and seeding seems pretty well sewn up.

Cal Quantrill touched 95.7 mph with his fastball, averaging 94.2 mph, and 95.9 mph with his sinker, averaging 94.0 mph. Tyler Alexander 's fastball reached 93.9 mph. Robert Garcia topped out at 94.7 mph with his fastball. Jacob Latz 's fastball maxed out at 96.8 mph.

Corey Seager's had a 110.3 mph home run, a 106.3 mph single, and a 105.8 mph single. Elias Diaz had a 109.6 mph line out. Evan Carter had a 105.8 mph fly out. Danny Jansen had a 104.4 mph double. Brandon Nimmo had a 102.5 mph single.

Now an off day before starting a nine game homestand. Let's spend the next 48 hours enjoying the win.

articles.title: 2026 Série D final draws crowd of 36,500
articles.summary: Parque do Sabiá, in Uberlândia, welcomed around 36,500 fans for the second leg of the 2026 Série D final between Uberlândia and ASACredits: Rafael Ribeiro/CB...
articles.body:
Parque do Sabiá, in Uberlândia, welcomed around 36,500 fans for the second leg of the 2026 Série D final between Uberlândia and ASA Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF

The Série D final between Uberlândia and ASA drew 36,500 fans this Sunday (13) and featured a great celebration in the stands. At Parque do Sabiá, a packed stadium witnessed Uberlândia's title over ASA, secured with a 2-0 win in Arapiraca (AL) and a 1-1 draw at home, as well as the champions' celebrations.

In 2025, Santa Cruz hosted the first match to decide the winner. Arena de Pernambuco, in São Lourenço da Mata (PE), welcomed 45,500 people. Despite the support, Barra-SC won 2-1 and then claimed the title with a goalless draw in Itajaí (SC).

In the 2019 edition, nearly 45,000 people watched Manaus x Brusque at Arena da Amazônia, in Manaus. The Amazonas and Santa Catarina sides drew 2-2 across the two matches, and Brusque took the title on penalties by a score of 6-5.

Parque do Sabiá, in Uberlândia, welcomed 36,500 fans for the second leg of the 2026 Série D final between Uberlândia and ASA Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF

Four years earlier, Albertão Stadium in Teresina had its stands filled by more than 40,000 people. On that occasion, River-PI was chasing the title against Botafogo-SP, but finished as runner-up after a goalless draw and failing to overturn the 3-2 loss in the first leg in Ribeirão Preto (SP).

In 2012, Sampaio Corrêa won Série D in front of more than 40,000 fans at Castelão, in São Luís, with a 2-0 victory over CRAC-GO. In the first match, in Catalão (GO).

Finally, in 2011, around 55,000 passionate Santa Cruz supporters backed the Cobra Coral in the final. Despite the fans' efforts, Tupi-MG were crowned champions, with another victory over the Pernambuco side, this time by 2-0 — the Minas Gerais team had come in off a 1-0 win.

With 44 years of history, the biggest venue in the interior of the state of Minas Gerais is located in the eastern area of the city of Uberlândia, the second most populous in Minas Gerais, with more than 710,000 inhabitants, according to the 2022 IBGE census — Belo Horizonte ranks first, with around 2.3 million.

Parque do Sabiá was inaugurated on May 27, 1982, the date it hosted Brazil 's 7-0 rout of Ireland — Sócrates (2), Serginho (2), Falcão , Luizinho and Zico all found the net. Besides marking the official opening, the match also set the stadium's attendance record: 72,733 spectators.

The venue also hosted a goalless draw between Brazil and Paraguay in the Copa América on October 20, 1983. Four years later, on December 9, Valdo and Renato secured a come-from-behind 2-1 win over Chile. Then, on May 28, 1991, the Seleção beat Bulgaria 3-0 in a friendly, with two goals from Neto and one from João Paulo.

articles.title: Payton Tolle starts with immaculate inning, Roman Anthony gets key hit as Red Sox beat Royals 4-1
articles.summary: Payton Tolle opened the game with an immaculate inning, Roman Anthony hit a go-ahead single and the Boston Red Sox beat the Kansas City Royals 4-1 on Sunday...
articles.body:
BOSTON (AP) — Payton Tolle opened the game with an immaculate inning , Roman Anthony hit a go-ahead single and the Boston Red Sox beat the Kansas City Royals 4-1 on Sunday in a game that's start was delayed by rain.

Tolle is the first Boston pitcher to throw an immaculate inning (three strikeouts on nine pitches) to start a game since Hall of Famer Pedro Martinez did it on May 18, 2002.

Caleb Durbin hit a solo homer and Trevor Story added a game-breaking two-run single for the Red Sox, who took the final two games of the three-game series.

Carter Jensen drove in the Royals' run with a pinch-hit single. Kansas City was looking for its first series win in Boston since 2017.

In the seventh, Anthony lined an opposite-field single against reliever Connor Thomas after Craig Kimbrel (1-5) walked the first two batters.

Garrett Whitlock (7-1) was credited with the victory. Aroldis Chapman got the final three outs for his 34th save and the 401st of his career.

Tolle, a hard-throwing 23-year-old left-hander, fanned Nick Loftin called, then got Bobby Witt Jr. and Jac Caglianone swinging in the first.

He went six scoreless innings, striking out seven while allowing four singles.

Noah Cameron gave up a run over six sharp innings.

Durbin belted Cameron's first pitch into the first row of seats above the Green Monster. Story's single came off Nate Pearson in the eighth.

Jensen's RBI single inside the first-base bag tied it.

The club announced Saturday that the finale's start time was pushed back 90 minutes due to the forecast of rain, which came and delayed the first pitch by 1 hour, 50 minutes.

Royals: RHP Michael Wacha (9-8, 3.25 ERA) is scheduled for the opener of a three-game series in Houston on Tuesday.

Red Sox: LHP Patrick Sandoval (1-5, 4.58) starts Tuesday in the series opener against Texas .

articles.title: How the Chargers lost to the Cardinals in Week 1's biggest upset
articles.summary: Here's a breakdown of how the Cardinals beat the Chargers.
articles.body:
Week 1 of the NFL season always seems to feature a surprising upset, and this year that win was courteous of the Arizona Cardinals .

While the Cardinals were expected to be one of the worst teams in the NFL this year, Arizona shocked the league by handling the Chargers in Los Angeles by a score of 26-14. Veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett and rookie running back Jeremiyah Love helped get Mike LaFleur his first win as the team's head coach.

The Chargers , meanwhile, face a long week wondering what happened this week. Los Angeles has Super Bowl aspirations after adding Mike McDaniel as the new offensive coordinator, but the offense sputtered by scoring just 14 points.

Here's a breakdown of how the Cardinals beat the Chargers.

The Chargers disappointing loss to the Cardinals began on the very first drive, when Arizona marched down the field and scored to take a 7-0 lead. That 70-yard drive heavily featured rookie running back Jeremiyah Love, who punched it in for his first NFL touchdown.

Following that drive, the Chargers tied the game with a touchdown drive of their own, which was then followed by a Cardinals missed field goal. It seemed like Los Angeles had settled into the game, but that came to a halt when Omarion Hampton fumbled in Cardinals territory to squander a scoring chance.

On the ensuing drive, the Cardinals got a field goal to take a 10-7 lead midway through the second quarter.

Entering halftime, the Chargers were down just three points but had the benefit of receiving the kickoff in the second half. Unfortunately, they failed to do much with the ball as the offense go just 19 yards before punting away. The Cardinals would add a field goal on the next drive, extending the lead to six points.

Los Angeles did produce a touchdown drive to follow, taking a 14-13 lead midway through the third quarter. That score stuck for a while with both teams trading punts for the next few drives, but the play of the game came when Arizona blocked a Chargers punt to get the ball deep in Los Angeles Territory, turning that into a touchdown.

The Cardinals took the lead 20-14, putting the Chargers on the ropes. Finally, Justin Herbert through his lone interception of the day on a deep attempt, which essentially put the game away for the Cardinals as Arizona got a field goal on its next possession.

The 23-14 deficit proved to be too much for the Chargers to overcome with such little time left in the game. Arizona added another three points to cement the win at 26-14.

Los Angeles was discombobulated on offense though the entire game, and the Chargers special teams had a nightmare play that swung the game. The Cardinals, however, punched above their weight to get Mike LaFleur his first win as a head coach.

articles.title: Lions, happy to escape Week 1 with win, know they must 'clean this up'
articles.summary: "We will clean this up, and there's a lot to clean up," Lions coach Dan Campbell told his team in the postgame locker room.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions beat the New Orleans Saints at Ford Field on Sunday, Sept. 13, in an game that nearly ended with the hosts completely blowing a three-possession lead. The Lions , at one point up by 21 points, had to force an incompletion on New Orleans ' two-point attempt in overtime to secure the win .

"We did not play our cleanest," Lions coach Dan Campbell said in the postgame locker room, per video posted by the team . "But when we had to have it, all three phases — it's what we talked about last night, man. When we needed somebody to pull us back out of the water ... we did that in all three phases. ... That was the difference, man."

Detroit's near-collapse started with 8:49 remaining in the third frame, when Saints quarterback Tyler Shough scrambled right and found wide receiver Chris Olave deep down the sideline for a 47-yard catch. The Saints converted on third down twice and scored eight plays after Olave's explosive gain.

The Saints scored and then kicked a field goal, then scored again, to send the game to overtime, where Amon-Ra St. Brown scored what eventually proved to be the game-winning touchdown. St. Brown was one of three players to earn a game ball from Campbell after the game, along with linebacker Derrick Barnes and wide receiver Tay Martin .

"I don't give a f--- if it's one point or it's f------ 30 points, it's a f------ dub," Goff said in the locker room. "Use this s--- for momentum, boys. I promise you, we're gonna get on a roll, look back at Week 1, at that f------ two-point stop, as the s--- that got us there."

Barnes had an interception and a sack, and Martin tallied three tackles on special teams, including a couple of impressive reps on punt coverage.

"In the NFL, man, most games you play come down to the wire, and if you can just find a way to win," defensive end Aidan Hutchinson , who had two sacks in the opener, told reporters after the game. "There's a lot of talent in this league. Just win. That's the mantra."

Added cornerback D.J. Reed : "You take an ugly win or a pretty loss any day."

The Lions have a short week, set to travel to Buffalo to play the Bills and quarterback Josh Allen on Thursday, Sept. 17. It's the Bills' first game in Highmark Stadium, which opened in June.

"We're going to clean this up," Campbell told his team. "The biggest thing is right now, guys, is you find a way to get the win, it's Week 1, and then you clean the s--- up. Because it feels a hell of a lot better than the loss to have to clean it up.

"That's the thing, we found a way to win. We will clean this up, and there's a lot to clean up."

articles.title: Top prospects Mitch Voit, Jonathan Santucci headline Mets' 2026 Player Development Awards
articles.summary: The Mets announced their 2026 Player Development Awards, honoring top prospects Mitch Voit as Player of the Year and Jonathan Santucci as Pitcher of the Year...
articles.body:
The Mets announced their 2026 Player Development Awards on Sunday with two top prospects headlining the honors.

They recognized infielder Mitch Voit as the Player of the Year and LHP Jonathan Santucci as the Pitcher of the Year.

Additionally among the player honors, outfielder Cleiner Ramirez was named the Mets ' DR Academy Player of the Year while RHP Abner Meza was named DR Academy Pitcher of the Year.

The recipients -- including field and gameplay coordinator David Adams (Minor League Staff Member of the Year), lead DSL hitting coach Bryce Wheary (DR Academy Staff Member of the Year) and senior scout Cesar Aranguren (Marlin McPhail Scout of the Year) -- are set to be honored in a pregame ceremony at Citi Field before Monday's 7:10 p.m. start on SNY against the Baltimore Orioles .

Voit, who turns 22 on Sept. 30, spent the 2026 season with High-A Brooklyn and Double-A Binghamton. In 29 games since his July 27 promotion, he slashed .347/.430/.517 with two home runs and 18 RBI.

Voit is No. 5 overall on the Mets' farm in SNY's latest ranking of the top 30 .

Santucci, 23, is the Mets' top pitching prospect on SNY's midseason list.

He earned his promotion from Binghamton to Triple-A Syracuse on July 28 after posting a 3.57 ERA in 19 games while striking out 120 and allowing an opposing batting average of .213. He has 37 strikeouts in seven starts over 29 innings with Syracuse.

articles.title: Tim Henman suggests what Ben Shelton needs to change after his US Open final defeat to Alexander Zverev
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev has continued his phenomenal season by beating Ben Shelton in the final of the US Open. Zverev is now a two-time Grand Slam...
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev has continued his phenomenal season by beating Ben Shelton in the final of the US Open.

Zverev is now a two-time Grand Slam champion, with the German having claimed his maiden title at this year's French Open.

The ATP number two, who also finished as runner-up at Wimbledon this summer, defeated Shelton 6-3, 7-6(7-2), 5-7, 6-2 in their highly anticipated US Open clash.

Zverev has since drawn praise from former British number one Tim Henman , who has more significantly suggested that the American should make a change to his game after this setback.

Ben Shelton told to make first serve more effective after US Open final loss

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis, Henman said: "When I look at the first serve percentage of Shelton (71%), I would sacrifice some of that to say I am going to go bigger and harder.

"When he changes the pace and hits the 110mph kicker or slider, it's much easier to get back. When you are hitting serves at 140mph that is a nightmare to get back.

"That is where Zverev has continued to serve so well and so consistently and his average first serve speed is much faster than Shelton's.

"I think that's something Shelton has to go away and think about with his team to say how can he make that first serve more effective?"

It was certainly a battle between two big servers at Arthur Ashe Stadium, where the home favorite failed to come out on top, much to the disappointment of the majority of the fans.

Alexander Zverev vs Ben Shelton US Open final serving stats

Along with the title, Zverev has earned $5.5 million in prize money, while he's also extending his head-to-head record with the American to 6-0.

Adding further comment on the match-up, Henman said: "You look at the head-to-head record and it's 5-0. I think they have played four tiebreaks and he has won all of them.

"In the biggest moments he is coming up with the best tennis. 30-30 and deuce, the first eight times Zverev was at either score on serve he won those points.

"So Shelton did not have a break point in either of those sets, it is such a good platform for Zverev to build from."

The New York battle between the ATP superstars lasted three hours and 33 minutes, with Shelton certainly threatening a comeback on home soil.

But he ultimately fell short of a major challenge to his opponent, who is also now leading the Race to Turin rankings after collecting 2,000 points.

articles.title: ‘Ultimate disrespect’ – Alexander Zverev’s Trinity Rodman moment draws strong reaction after US Open win
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev’s post-match banter with Trinity Rodman, the US soccer star and Ben Shelton’s girlfriend, caught the attention of fans after he defeated the...
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev's post-match banter with Trinity Rodman, the US soccer star and Ben Shelton's girlfriend, caught the attention of fans after he defeated the home favourite to win the second Grand Slam title of his career in the same year.

Zverev beat Shelton 6-3, 7-6 (7-2), 5-7, 6-2 in front of his home crowd to win his second Grand Slam title, becoming the second German after Boris Becker to win a US Open crown.

Alexander Zverev's Trinity Rodman banter gets fans talking

After the game was done and dusted, Zverev was on the mic thanking everyone before turning his attention to Rodman. The German asked her about her game before joking about her being Shelton's lucky charm, leading to a fun exchange between the two.

"Hey Trinity, I thought you have a game today, no? Well done to you as well. You're the lucky charm, so. Not today, but usually," Zverev joked.

ESPN shared a video of the moment on social media, and the exchange quickly prompted reactions from fans, with some viewing Zverev's comment as a particularly bold move after defeating Shelton in the final.

One fan wrote: "Beats him for the title, now trying to steal his gal. Cold."

Another fan simply called it: "The ultimate disrespect by Zverev."

A third fan took things further, writing: "Nah if I'm Ben I'm punching on Zverev. You ain't gonna embarrass me in the final and then be flirting with my girl like that. Oh hell nah."

Another person reacted: "Bro beat him and took a shot at his girl. Pure humiliation."

A fifth fan wrote: "Bro won the Grand Slam trophy and still found time to drop a stray comment. Coldest line of the entire tournament."

articles.title: Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen dominates coverage in Week 1 victory
articles.summary: Riq Woolen saw four targets but allowed no catches or yards over 37 coverage snaps in his first start for the Philadelphia Eagles
articles.body:
Riq Woolen could not have provided a much stronger introduction to fans in the City of Brotherly Love during his first regular-season start with the Philadelphia Eagles . According to Ryan Fowler of NBC Sports Philadelphia , Woolen was targeted four times during Philadelphia's 24-22 victory over the Washington Commanders . He did not allow a reception or a receiving yard across 37 coverage snaps.

Washington tested other areas of Philadelphia's secondary throughout the game, but Jayden Daniels found little success when directing the football toward Woolen. The Commanders quarterback completed 18 of 34 passes for 164 yards and two touchdowns. The performance illustrated why Philadelphia identified Woolen as an unquestioned starter after signing him to a one-year contract during the offseason.

At 6-foot-4, Woolen gives defensive coordinator Vic Fangio a rare combination of size, length, and recovery speed at outside cornerback. His physical traits let him disrupt receivers at the line of scrimmage while still able to recover when opponents test him vertically.

Philadelphia's secondary produced some uneven moments elsewhere. Cooper DeJean allowed a fourth-quarter touchdown to Stefon Diggs from the slot, while Washington moved within two points during the final minute.

Woolen remained steady throughout those difficulties. His coverage helped force Daniels to hold the football, move through his progressions, or target more favorable matchups on the opposite side.

One performance does not answer every question about Woolen's fit in Fangio's defense, but his debut represented an ideal beginning. If Woolen can consistently eliminate one side of the field, Philadelphia will have greater freedom to disguise coverages and direct safety help elsewhere.

articles.title: New AP Poll Top 25 punishes Ohio State, Oklahoma, Oregon, Texas jumps to No 1 after big comeback
articles.summary: The AP Top 25 poll reshuffled after Texas Longhorns topped Ohio State, but the Buckeyes' five-spot drop exposes a flaw in how voters weigh losses.
articles.body: Week two of the college football season delivered another series of typically chaotic results. And the College Football Playoff picture has already shifted, thanks to several surprising outcomes. The Oregon Ducks were expected to compete for a Big Ten Championship with the Ohio State Buckeyes and Indiana Hoosiers, only to barely escape against Boise State and get deservedly beaten by Oklahoma State. The Cowboys' in-state rivals, the Oklahoma Sooners, lost on the road at Michigan, scoring just 10 points in the process. Those Wolverines, left for dead after the asterisk-laden win over Western Michigan in week one, are suddenly right back in the playoff picture after beating a top-11 SEC opponent. And of course, the Texas Longhorns won the game of the year over Ohio State, giving them a huge resume boost and a substantial leg up should they need an at-large playoff berth. This week's AP Top 25 Poll reflects some of that chaos, while also providing a good example of the flaws with the "some wins are better than some losses" perspective shared by such figures as Nick Saban. Here are this week's rankings, and what it means for the rest of the season. One of the obvious takeaways? articles.title: Who is Joanna Wietrzyk? Australian HYROX athlete and fitness coach at centre of Beijing controversy

articles.body: Australian athlete Joanna Wietrzyk has become the focus of attention after a controversial finish at the HYROX Beijing fitness race on September 12, 2026. Wietrzyk, who competed in the Women’s Pro division, reportedly suffered bowel incontinence during the race but continued through the course and finished in 1:01:23. The incident drew strong reactions because HYROX uses shared running lanes and workout equipment, including rowing machines, sleds and mats. HYROX China said the affected area was isolated and disinfected, while equipment was removed and replaced. The organizer did not publicly name the athlete in its statement.Who is Joanna Wietrzyk? Australian HYROX athlete and fitness coachJoanna Wietrzyk is an Australian elite fitness racing athlete, strength and conditioning coach and competitor in the international HYROX and functional fitness scene. She has a background in CrossFit, functional bodybuilding and competitive athletics before moving into hybrid endurance racing.Wietrzyk competes in the Women’s Pro division, the higher-level category of HYROX competition. Her races combine running with workout stations, and she has built a reputation for strong performances across the sled and ergometer sections. In 2026, she competed at major events including Phoenix, Warsaw and the World Championships. She won the Warsaw Major and set the Women’s Solo Pro world record with 54:25.Away from competition, Wietrzyk works as an online performance coach and personal trainer. Her work includes race preparation, hybrid endurance and strength training.What happened to Joanna Wietrzyk at HYROX Beijing?The controversy began after photos and videos from the September 12 HYROX Beijing event spread on social media. They appeared to show Wietrzyk continuing to race after suffering bowel incontinence. She carried on with movements including burpees, and reports said the incident affected parts of the course and equipment used by athletes behind her.That led to two different reactions. Some people praised Wietrzyk for finishing despite an extremely difficult moment. Others questioned why the race continued while shared areas and equipment could have been affected. The debate also raised questions about how HYROX should handle a hygiene or safety problem during a live race.HYROX China responded on September 12, saying the affected area and lanes were sealed off and isolated as soon as possible. The organizer said it carried out full disinfection through the end of the day’s events and removed and replaced the relevant equipment. It also said the entire carpet would be replaced after the competition, followed by deep cleaning and disinfection.Reports identifying the athlete as Wietrzyk also said she won the Women’s Pro race in 1:01:23. HYROX’s official event page confirms that the Women’s Pro race took place on September 12, but its public event information does not identify Wietrzyk in connection with the incident.After the race, Wietrzyk reportedly shared a hospital-bed selfie with the message, “A win is a win.” The post added another layer to the online debate, with some readers seeing it as determination and others questioning the decision to continue racing.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Sophie Cunningham had already played her part in the Indiana Fever’s 112-98 win over the Portland Fire on Friday, August 1, 2026. But the moment that stayed with fans came after the final buzzer. Cunningham walked toward a young Fever supporter in the stands and handed her one of her game-worn shoes. The girl looked stunned, then covered her face as the emotion hit her.The Indiana Fever later shared the moment on social media, and the young fan’s reaction quickly drew attention. She did not simply take the shoe and move on. She looked at it in disbelief before becoming visibly emotional. For Cunningham, it was a quick postgame gesture. For the young supporter, it became a memory tied to a Fever win she will likely never forget. Sophie Cunningham noticed a young fan and gave her a game-worn shoe after the Fever’s 112-98 winThe moment came at the end of a busy night for Cunningham in Portland. She had dealt with boos from sections of the Moda Center crowd when she entered the game midway through the first quarter. Rather than let the reception affect her, she answered with a three-pointer and finished with 13 points as Indiana picked up its fifth straight victory.Then came the part nobody could have planned. After the final buzzer, Cunningham walked toward the stands and handed a young Fever fan her game-worn shoe. The child immediately looked overwhelmed. In the video shared by the Fever on August 1, she appeared to stare at the shoe in disbelief before putting her hands over her face.The Fever highlighted that exact reaction in its social media post, writing, “The reaction on this young fan’s face when Sophie Cunningham gifted her a game-worn shoe after tonight’s win in Portland.”It was a fitting way to end a night that had already given Fever fans plenty to celebrate. Indiana scored 112 points, with Caitlin Clark leading the way with 26 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists. Kelsey Mitchell also scored 26, while the Fever pulled away with a 34-point third quarter. The victory marked Indiana’s fifth consecutive win, and the team became the first in WNBA history to score at least 100 points in five straight games.But the young fan’s reaction shifted the focus from the scoreboard to something much more personal.Fever fans praised Sophie Cunningham for giving the young supporter a memory she will never forgetThe reaction did not stop with the video. Fans flooded the Fever’s post with messages praising Cunningham for taking the time to connect with a young supporter.One fan wrote, “How beautiful is this amazing woman, inside and out! She's Phenominal!!”Another folk added, “You will be remembered for being on the right side of history @sophaller.”One fan even admitted that Cunningham had changed their feelings about the Fever, writing, “I usually only root for New York teams, but @sophaller has made me a fan of the Indiana Fever, simply because she’s an amazing person, God Bless!”Another fan thanked Cunningham for the way she interacts with supporters, writing, “Thank you Sophie for always standing up for what is right and being there for the fans. I wish more athletes had your strength and moral courage. You will inspire many more.”There was also a lighter reaction to the postgame interaction. One fan joked about Cunningham using her long reach for a selfie, writing, “Sophie's like ‘obviously we'll use my extra-long arms to take a selfie’ 🤣 She's a gem.”Cunningham’s shoe may have been just another piece of equipment after a WNBA game. articles.title: Dhiraj Bommadevara becomes first Indian male recurve archer to win World Cup final gold medal in shoot-off thriller
articles.summary: More sports News: Top-ranked Indian recurve archer Dhiraj Bommadevara created history on Sunday by becoming the first Indian male recurve archer to win gold at the Arch.
articles.body: Top-ranked Indian recurve archer Dhiraj Bommadevara created history on Sunday by becoming the first Indian male recurve archer to win gold at the Archery World Cup Final, beating Japan's Nakanishi Junya in a shoot-off in Saltillo, Mexico.After finishing without a medal in the 2023 and 2024 editions, the 25-year-old Army man from Vijayawada produced his best run at the World Cup Final. He reached the final after wins in the quarterfinals and semifinals before defeating world No. 20 Junya 6-5 (28-28, 28-29, 29-28, 28-30, 28-27). With the match tied 5-5 after five sets, Dhiraj won the shoot-off 10-9.With the victory, Dhiraj became the first Indian male recurve archer to win gold at the World Cup Final. He also ended a 16-year wait for an Indian male recurve archer to win a medal at the event. Jayanta Talukdar was the last Indian man to finish on the podium, winning bronze in Edinburgh in 2010.Dola Banerjee remains the only other Indian to have won World Cup Final gold, claiming the women's individual title in Dubai in 2007. No Indian had won gold at the World Cup Final since then.Deepika Kumari, however, remains India's most successful archer at the World Cup Final with five silver medals and one bronze from eight appearances.Dhiraj will now head to Japan for the Asian Games, where he will lead India's recurve campaign. At the Hangzhou Asian Games, he was knocked out in the quarterfinals of the individual event but won a team silver medal.In the gold medal match, Dhiraj twice trailed Junya before fighting back. The Japanese archer, who had knocked out Tokyo Olympics champion Mete Gazoz in the semifinal, dropped only three points from his first six arrows to take a 3-1 lead.Dhiraj responded with a score of 29 in the third set to level the match at 3-3. Junya then shot a perfect three-arrow set in the fourth to move 5-3 ahead and needed only a tied fifth set to win the gold.The Indian kept his composure in the deciding set, scoring 28 while Junya managed 27, forcing a shoot-off. Dhiraj then hit a perfect 10, while Junya scored 9, sealing the biggest title of his career.Earlier, Dhiraj beat Rio Olympics silver medallist Jean-Charles Valladont of France 7-1 (28-25, 28-28, 29-24, 29-28) in the semifinal without losing a set.He had opened his campaign with a 7-1 win over Turkey's Berkim Tumer in the quarterfinals (28-25, 29-26, 28-28). Dhiraj dropped only two points with his first three arrows and took a 4-0 lead after the second set before a tied third set confirmed his place in the semifinals.This was Dhiraj's second semifinal appearance at the World Cup Final. On his debut in Hermosillo in 2023, he had reached the semifinals before losing the bronze-medal playoff.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: A coach's fasting, nod to MS Dhoni, and the 'funniest' team: Inside Ganges Grandmasters' GCL 2026 title
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: Who doesn't love a good underdog story? Everyone does, right? Nobody had Ganges Grandmasters finishing on top of anything when Season 4 of .
articles.body: BENGALURU: Who doesn't love a good underdog story? Everyone does, right? Nobody had Ganges Grandmasters finishing on top of anything when Season 4 of the Global Chess League (GCL) began in Bengaluru just less than a fortnight ago. Six teams, a league stage so tight, and a final that only got decided after the very last match was played on Saturday evening.With Grandmasters like Ian Nepomniachtchi, Levon Aronian, Leinier Domínguez and Leon Luke Mendonca, and International Masters like Polina Shuvalova and Stavroula Tsolakidou, it was a diverse side, one few expected to go all the way.By Sunday, as the confetti cannons went off, it was Ganges Grandmasters, not the defending champions APL Pipers, not the team with Magnus Carlsen on the Icon board, standing at the top of the podium.7-5 remained the aggregate score by which Ganges Grandmasters beat the Pipers across the two-leg final, having drawn the first leg 3-3, where the Grandmasters played with the White pieces.With the Black, though, Ian Nepomniachtchi pounced on a positional error from Carlsen, refusing to give the world number one any route back into the game. And as the five-time world champion's position collapsed, so did the Pipers' hopes of retaining the title. Behind the scenes, however, the triumph is about so much more than a good underdog story.A 'not a full-time coach' at the helmAdhiban Baskaran, who, by the admission of all the players in the team, played an integral role in keeping it all together throughout the campaign, is not a coach."I'm not a full-time coach, so I wanted to clarify. I am like a professional player," the 34-year-old Grandmaster told reporters on Sunday. "But this time, I was free. I didn't have any tournaments in September, so I just wanted to be part of something great."That "something great" turned into a maiden GCL title on debut as a coach, a fact Baskaran still seemed slightly stunned by."To win the GCL Season 4 on debut is amazing, and something I'm very proud of," he added.What makes his version of the story worth telling isn't the tactics or the pairings. It's what he brought into the dugout that had nothing to do with chess at all.With his humour, superstition, and a level of emotional investment, he uplifted the overall spirit of the team after a topsy-turvy start to the tournament, including two wins and two losses in the opening four games.Take the nickname, for example. Somewhere along the way, Baskaran started handing out monikers to the squad, and one of them, nevertheless, became more popular than the others.Earlier in the tournament, Greek chess player Stavroula Tsolakidou revealed that Baskaran had prepared her for a game with a file titled “Prep for the Greek Goddess!”"I was trying to come up with nicknames for everyone, and that's how I came up with this nickname, Greek Goddess," he said. It became a name that would end up being shouted across the venue by the time she clinched the title-sealing win over Koneru Humpy and picked up the Player of the Tournament award, complete with a Jawa motorbike."I didn't expect it would actually become so popular in such a short span," Baskaran admitted.Then there was the fasting. After a mid-tournament loss, Baskaran quietly made himself a promise."I didn't have breakfast, I didn't have lunch, and I told myself if the team is not winning, I will also not have dinner," he said with a smile after Sunday's victory. "And they won. So I could actually have dinner."What started as a one-off superstition calcified into a five-day ritual."I thought, okay, why fix something which doesn't break? So I started to fast every lunch. I didn't have lunch for the past five days, also with the thought that I would not have dinner if the team didn't win. But luckily, my team was always winning, and they were helping me, so I could at least have dinner," he revealed.By the end of the tournament, he was only half-joking about the toll it had taken. "My stomach is literally crying now," he remarked.An accidental nod to MS DhoniBaskaran's calm in the dugout, it turns out, had a specific origin, and it arrived by text message, from his father, in the middle of the rough patch earlier in the season."After the second day, I think we lost one match," Baskaran recalled. "And my father sent me this message that, you know, you just try to be like one of your role models, Dhoni. He messaged, 'Try to be like Captain Cool, your role model.' So I was like, yeah, I will try to be like that.""In fact, I chose my (jersey) number seven for Ronaldo," he said. "But actually, Dhoni's number is also seven. So there's an inside joke about Dhoni; the credit always walks back to Dhoni."Pressed on whether that same reflexive credit-giving applied here, the way, say, cricketer Hardik Pandya once attributed India wins to Dhoni's mere presence in the dressing room, Baskaran deflected the comparison entirely."No, no. Here I feel it's because of my team," he added. "I think they played very well."Whatever the jersey number said, Baskaran's dugout stayed visibly, deliberately calm, right up until it had a trophy to celebrate.A childhood hero, now a champion teammateBaskaran admits that the real reason he chose to coach the GCL outfit during his time off had little to do with money, fame, or anything material."Levon (Aronian) has been my hero for as long as I can remember," Baskaran revealed. "Ever since he won the World Junior in Goa, I've been a big fan of him." Getting to coach him, rather than simply admire him from a distance, was its own reward. "Getting to understand how the players are, the psychology, how they prepare, that's something I really wanted to know. So that was the reason I wanted to be part of this team."Aronian, for his part, returned the affection when asked about Baskaran directly."He's such a friendly, such a calm and pleasant person," Aronian said after the trophy celebration. "I've known him since he was very young, even our fathers are friends."Throughout the tournament, this did not look like a group of mercenaries assembled for a tournament, as confirmed by Aronian as well."I think we have very relaxed egos, less structure in a team, and everybody can make a joke. There is no limit to jokes. I just felt like it was some family type of experience. I will treasure those days," the veteran Grandmaster admitted.Russian Grandmaster and the team's icon player Nepomniachtchi, whose demolition of Carlsen effectively won the title, echoed the same sentiment from a very different starting point, a player who admitted he'd arrived in Bengaluru unsure of his own form after a rough year of rating losses."I wasn't sure what my form was at the moment," he said. "But I was really pleasantly surprised with the atmosphere inside the team. Despite different ages, different cultures, we really found points of connection. It was always very healthy, very jokey. I think it really made the difference."'The funniest team' wins it finallyGoing by their social media, one can see the Ganges Grandmasters players often indulging in physical sports like padel, golf, and basketball after their gruelling round of matches in GCL. Perhaps that built the team spirit."I think it's more about team spirit," Adhiban said. "Always joking, always having fun, I would actually say we are the funniest team. Maybe that's one of the reasons."Nobody had Ganges Grandmasters in their top two.By Sunday night, the top belonged to the man who led the underdogs, now holding a trophy, still fasting, still cracking jokes in the "funniest team" of the GCL's fourth edition. articles.title: India’s three-sport Asian Games mission: Bullseyes, knockout punches and golden arrows
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: India’s Asian Games stories are often written in gold, silver and bronze. But behind the numbers lies a more compelling narrative: the stil.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s Asian Games stories are often written in gold, silver and bronze. But behind the numbers lies a more compelling narrative: the stillness of a shooter before the trigger breaks, the controlled fury of a boxer inside the ropes, and the unblinking concentration of an archer waiting for the perfect release. As Aichi-Nagoya approaches, these three disciplines once again stand at the heart of India’s medal ambitions.Shooting has evolved from a promising pursuit into one of the country’s most dependable continental medal engines. Maharaja Karni Singh’s silver in the clay pigeon trap at Tehran in 1974 marked India’s first Asian Games medal in shooting. Decades later, the sport’s legacy is carried by names such as the late Jaspal Rana, whose pistol dominance defined multiple editions, and Abhinav Bindra, whose Olympic triumph helped elevate Indian marksmanship to a global stage.The watershed moment came at Hangzhou in 2023. Indian shooters collected a record 22 medals — seven gold, nine silver and six bronze — across rifle, pistol and shotgun events. The campaign was a statement of depth as much as excellence. Divyansh Singh Panwar, Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar and Rudrankksh Patil combined for a world-record-setting team gold in the men’s 10m air rifle, while Sift Kaur Samra and Palak Gulia added individual gold.Aichi-Nagoya brings a 30-member squad, evenly divided between men and women, with Manu Bhaker at its centre. The double Olympic medallist’s presence gives the pistol section a formidable edge, alongside Esha Singh and veteran Rahi Sarnobat. Rifle fire power comes from Rudrankksh and Elavenil Valarivan, while Kynan Chenai leads the shotgun challenge. The target is not simply to repeat Hangzhou, but to prove that India’s shooting bench has become deep enough to sustain success.But the new campaign also carries a reminder that past glory guarantees nothing. Sift Kaur, Swapnil Kusale and Sarabjot Singh, the Hangzhou gold medallists in pistol and rifle events, are among the notable names missing from the squad. Their absence underlines the intensity of selection and the changing nature of India’s shooting bench.From the firing line, the narrative moves to the ring, where precision must survive pressure, punches and the judgment of three rounds. Indian boxing’s Asian Games journey began with medals for Sundar Rao and Hari Singh in 1958. Hawa Singh’s consecutive heavyweight golds in 1966 and 1970 established an early standard; Mary Kom’s 2014 triumph made her the first Indian woman to win Asian Games boxing gold, while Amit Panghal’s 2018 victory remains India’s most recent men’s gold.The numbers underline both achievement and unfinished business: nine gold, 17 silver and 35 bronze medals, according to the historical tally supplied for India’s boxing record. Hangzhou yielded five medals — one silver and four bronze — but Aichi-Nagoya arrives after a stirring Commonwealth Games campaign in Glasgow, where Indian boxers won seven gold and three silver. Yet the Asian Games will be a much sterner examination. Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, China, Japan and North Korea bring the continent’s deepest boxing traditions. As Boxing Federation of India president Ajay Singh put it, the Asian Games are “like the Olympics”. The test is whether India’s recent resurgence can withstand the very best.Lovlina Borgohain carries experience and authority. Alongside her, Sakshi Chaudhary, Preeti Pawar, Priya Ghanghas and Sachin Siwach represent a generation that has already tasted success. The challenge is to convert momentum into medals when every bout is a continental crossroads.And then comes archery, where India’s rise has been astonishingly swift. However, the game will have its absences in 2026. Ojas Pravin Deotale, who won three golds at Hangzhou has missed selection. The omission of established names such as Atanu Das, Deepika Kumari and Abhishek Verma further highlights the changing landscape.The three sports share a common demand: the ability to remain composed when the moment becomes enormous. A trigger, a punch and an arrow may seem worlds apart, yet each discipline has the firepower to swell India’s medal tally under the brightest continental spotlight.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El Grande Americano Beats Dom Mysterio to Win Mega Title in Historic WWE x AAA Triplemania 34
articles.summary: El Grande Americano beat Dominik Mysterio in the main event of Night 2 of Triplemanía 34 in Mexico City on Sunday to win the AAA Mega Championship.
articles.body:
El Grande Americano beat Dominik Mysterio in the main event of Night 2 of Triplemanía 34 in Mexico City on Sunday to win the AAA Mega Championship.

Over the past year, El Grande Americano has established himself as one of the biggest stars in all of lucha libre, and Sunday represented the most significant opportunity of his career.

Americano earned a future shot at the AAA Mega Championship at Rey de Reyes back in March, but it took some time before he got to cash in on that opportunity.

That is primarily due to the fact that he first had to conclude his rivalry with the original El Grande Americano, resulting in a mask vs. mask match at Noche de Los Grandes in May.

Grande won what was among the best matches of the year in all of pro wrestling, and the original El Grande Americano was revealed to be Chade Gable.

After that, Grande's focus shifted toward Dirty Dom and the AAA Mega Championship, and it wasn't long before his feud with Mysterio became a heated one.

During a tag team match against Los Perros del Mal, Dominik turned his back on Grande and allowed him to be outnumbered. Shortly thereafter, Dom stacked the deck in his favor even more by aligning himself with Dorian Roldán and Omos.

While Dom was once a favorite of the Mexican crowd, El Grande Americano won them over in the months leading up to Triplemanía, making Mysterio the clear heel.

A Grande win was far from guaranteed, though, as Dominik entered Triplemanía with a yearlong title reign and a willingness to do anything in order to keep the belt.

Despite that, El Grande Americano secured the biggest victory of his career on Sunday, much to the delight of the fans in Mexico City.

articles.title: Josiah Trotter has Historic Debut in Buccaneers Loss
articles.summary: Buccaneers rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter made history on Sunday, becoming the only player in NFL history to record a pick-six and a sack in his debut.
articles.body:
Rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter had a historic debut for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday.

Unfortunately, Trotter's tremendous performance came in a Tampa loss. Three lost fumbles by quarterback Baker Mayfield doomed the Bucs in their 33-27 road loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.

While the turnovers dug the Bucs a hole they couldn't crawl out of, Trotter was a monster for Tampa's defense.

Greg Auman of Fox Sports reported that Trotter became the first player in NFL history with both a pick-six and a sack in his debut.

Just for good measure, Trotter also threw in 11 tackles, a pair of TFLs, and even broke up a pass. Not too shabby.

The game against the Bengals meant the long wait for the most-anticipated debut by a Bucs rookie in a long time was finally over.

First-round pick Rueben Bain Jr., who has looked like a superstar since coming to town, was supposed to be the Tampa rookie who dominated on Sunday. Instead, the star edge rusher from Miami showed up on the stat sheet with just one tackle.

Not the debut from Bain that many expected, though it's possible nothing he could have done against the Bengals would have matched the hype and expectations he's earned for himself this offseason.

Instead, it was Trotter who stole the show for Tampa's defense. If not for his Herculean effort, who knows how much worse this loss could have been?

The rookie inside linebacker was drafted in the second round and didn't come with nearly the same attention Bain did. Even though the Bucs also had high expectations for Trotter , he spent the offseason being overshadowed by Bain, no matter how well he had been playing.

After Sunday's performance, Trotter will no longer be overshadowed. Not by Bain or anybody else on Tampa's defense.

Although Bain entered the season as the favorite to win Defensive Rookie of the Year , he may receive some unexpected competition to be the best rookie on his own team.

Sunday was a remarkable debut from Trotter. He was the best player on the field for the Bucs all afternoon. It's a shame that his performance didn't lead to a victory.

Next week, Trotter and the Bucs take on the Cleveland Browns . After seeing how the Browns looked in their 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, Trotter must be licking his chops.

What will the rookie have in store for his encore?

We will have to wait a week to find out.

articles.title: 49ers Called Top Trade Fit for Disgruntled AFC Star
articles.summary: ESPN called the San Francisco 49ers the top trade fit for 1 disgruntled AFC star. The post 49ers Called Top Trade Fit for Disgruntled AFC Star appeared first...
articles.body:
If the Pittsburgh Steelers are truly looking to move star cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a trade instead of paying him, only a few teams have what it takes to get him — namely, the proper draft capital and the proper amount of salary cap space.

The San Francisco 49ers are 1 of those teams, which ESPN's Jeremy Fowler pointed out, and put them at the top of his list of trade fits for Porter after he sat out the season-opening win over the Atlanta Falcons .

"The 49ers' cornerback rotation looked stout Thursday against the Los Angeles Rams , but seasons are long and Porter would help the defense immensely," Fowler wrote on Sunday, September 13. " San Francisco has eight draft picks in 2027 and around $45 million in cap space. Porter Jr. opposite Deommodore Lenoir would form a stout 1-2 cornerback combo for the 49ers."

What Would it Cost to Trade for Joey Porter Jr.?

The cost to bring Porter Jr. to the Commanders would be something along the lines of a 2027 3rd-round pick or a 2028 2nd-round pick.

"Porter has maintained his desire to be compensated as a top-level corner, a position that has seen five players reach or eclipse the $30 million per year mark since the start of last offseason, including a record-setting four-year, $133 million contract for Seattle Seahawks star Devon Witherspoon ," Bleacher Report's Alex Kay wrote on August 25. "While Porter probably won't reset the market, he's due for a major raise over the $4 million in base salary he's due in 2026. The corner has been a lynchpin in Pittsburgh's secondary since being drafted No. 32 overall in 2023. In that span, the second-rounder has appeared in 41 games — starting 41 — and recorded 165 tackles, 31 pass defenses and three interceptions."

Joey Porter Jr. Son of Legendary NFL Linebacker

If you didn't guess already, Porter Jr. is the son of legendary NFL linebacker Joey Porter, a 4-time NFL All-Pro and Pro Bowler who helped lead the Steelers to a Super Bowl victory following the 2005 season.

After becoming a 3-time All-Big Ten pick at Penn State, Porter Jr. was projected as a 1st-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft but dropped to the 1st pick of the 2nd round at No. 32 overall.

In his 1st 3 seasons, Porter Jr. has started 41 out of the 47 regular-season games he's played in, but missed a career-high 3 games in 2025.

Steelers fans do not want Porter going anywhere, but not getting that big paycheck at this point is a sign things have gone south.

"We were looking for a number 1 corner for years lol no way we trade him," Steelers fan JermPGH wrote on his official X account. "I definitely get why teams would check in."

articles.title: The silver medal Koneru Humpy's 9-year-old daughter will remember as gold
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: While her father sat in the VIP lounge at the Lalit Ashok on Sunday, talking through what it means to be married to one of India's most res.
articles.body: BENGALURU: While her father sat in the VIP lounge at the Lalit Ashok on Sunday, talking through what it means to be married to one of India's most respected grandmasters, nine-year-old Ahana wasn't interested in any of that. Her mind was only on the playing arena metres away, where Koneru Humpy and her team, APL Pipers, were fighting for the Global Chess League (GCL) title against the Ganges Grandmasters.As the pair was waiting for the match passes to reach them, she kept nudging her father, Dasari Anvesh, to take her closer, down from the lounge, into the hall, near enough to actually watch her mother play live. Remarkably, this was the first time in her young life she was going to see her mother play a competitive game of chess in person."This is our first edition of GCL," Anvesh told TimesofIndia.com, smiling as he recalled this was his second after a tournament in Russia. "We're visiting physically, and the good thing is Humpy's team is in the final. So it's very exciting times."Asked if she had a message for her mother before the match began, the shyness in the nine-year-old took over; she perhaps didn't quite know what to say to someone she was about to watch, for the first time, not as a mother at home but as a competitor on a stage.It's a distinction her father has lived inside for over a decade.Just this year, Humpy withdrew from the Women's Candidates in Cyprus, the tournament that stands between a player and a shot at the World Championship title, citing safety concerns amid the tensions in the Middle East."It was a collective family decision," Anvesh revealed. "The time was not right. Whenever she wants to play any game, we always support her wherever she wants to go. But at that time, we all felt safety comes first, and we took that decision collectively, even though it was very challenging."Humpy, he added, "stuck to that, and gave importance to family."It's the same trade-off that has run through their marriage since 2014, and deepened three years later when Ahana was born and Humpy stepped away from the board for a stretch."Humpy is able to balance both sport and family," Anvesh said. "Whenever there's a tournament, she's fully focused and playing for it. But whenever she's out of the tournament, she always gives priority to family, spending time with me, with our kid.""As a mother, as a wife, she's giving her hundred per cent. Family comes first, and then sport. Even when she was pregnant, she took a sabbatical. She has a lot of importance for family, and her passion for chess always drives her, it's nice to see her balancing it so well."He was quick to redirect any credit for her game away from himself. "I'm not a chess player. My father-in-law is the main coach who has trained Humpy," he acknowledged. "All credit goes to him. I was the only one staying calm and offering emotional support."One result, two different reactionsOn Sunday, Humpy's team ended on the losing side. Stavroula Tsolakidou, playing Black, beat her in the decisive game that handed the title to Ganges Grandmasters, leaving Humpy and her Pipers side with silver.At the medal ceremony, Ahana and her father had the front-row seats, watching her mother step up to receive the silver.For Humpy, a player with close to three decades of medals in every colour, it will register the way these things always do for someone who has spent a career one step from the top. Another near-miss, a missed shot at gold on a competitive stage.For Ahana, sitting in the front row as the medal was placed around her mother's neck, it didn't register that way at all.Clapping alongside her father, she looked like she might lose her balance from sheer joy.She was perhaps not clapping for the silver medal. She was clapping because her mother had just finished playing and received a prize for that, live, in front of her, for the very first time. It must have been a whirlwind of emotions for her.Somewhere in that gap is the actual story of this final. Humpy, disappointed after the result, was hardly smiling. Ahana, however, was all smiles as she made her way out of the playing venue, clutching her father's hand.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Blue Devils Exact Revenge Against Stanford in Rout
articles.summary: Stanford's unbeaten run ends on the road against Duke in convincing fashion.
articles.body:
The Stanford Cardinal women's soccer program came into Sunday's pivotal matchup with No. 3 Duke at a bit of a disadvantage , and the Blue Devils ended up with a 5-0 rout at home, defeating the previously unbeaten Cardinal in convincing fashion.

Stanford still has six players missing due to the U-20 World Cup in Poland, while Duke does not have a single player on the U.S. team. They also had some extra motivation in this one, not only playing at home against the top-ranked program in the country, but also facing Stanford, the team that eliminated Duke from the College Cup in 2025, just shy of the national championship game.

Last season, Stanford lost its first match to then-ranked No. 18 UCLA 2-0 on September 7, so the Cardinal are in a similar spot this season record-wise. Last year's program also went on a run at that point, not losing a single game until the national title match.

On Sunday, Duke got the scoring started early with Katie Shea Collins notching her sixth goal of the season in the 15th minute. She would assist on Duke's next two goals in the 36th and 52nd minutes, scored by Avery Oder (4th) and Yuna Marui (1st).

Marui would assist on Duke's fourth goal of the match in the 59th minute, and Oder would score the fifth and final goal on a penalty kick in the 79th minute.

Right before Stanford lost a number of players to the U-20, we noted that the Cardinal had been doing a tremendous job defensively in limiting the number of shot attempts the opposition receives, which is a surefire way to limit how many goals they can score.

For the first time this season, Stanford was outshot by an opponent, with Duke leading the way 13-12. Duke goalkeeper Molly Vapensky was terrific in net, recording five saves to secure the clean sheet. This was a tough draw for Stanford's backup goaltender Rhiannon Stewart, with All-ACC goaltender Caroline Birkel away.

The loss drops Stanford to 6-1-1 on the season and 0-1-0 in ACC play, while Duke picks up a huge win, now sitting at 6-0-1 and 1-0-0 in conference play.

Stanford's next match will be at home on Thursday, September 17 against Louisville. The Cardinals are 7-1 this season, dropping a match to Nebraska in the season opener, but they have rattled off seven straight wins since, meaning another tough test for the shorthanded Cardinal program is coming up.

articles.title: Yankees Are Giving Bettors Plenty of Reasons to Believe
articles.summary: The New York Yankees are closing the gap on the LA Dodgers, but the market still isn't fully convinced at this point. The post Yankees Are Giving Bettors Ple...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are still the team everyone has to beat. But the New York Yankees are giving bettors plenty of reasons to believe that somebody else could finally end their reign.

The Dodgers remain the clear favorites to win the World Series with Oddscheckers listing them at +175, giving them an implied 36% probability of winning it all. That would make a third consecutive championship and the 10th World Series title in franchise history.

Yet the betting market is starting to rally behind the Yankees.

New York is sitting at +700, good for a 13% implied probability, but it has attracted an enormous 40% of the World Series wagers received this week.

As Oddschecker spokesman Chris Rogers explained, "Bettors are rallying behind the NY Yankees for the World Series this week. At +700, the Yankees have received 40% of World Series wagers. LA Dodgers continue to lead the betting at +175 and have a 36% implied chance of clinching a landmark 10th World Series title."

That's why there is a reason for that optimism.

The Yankees have been remarkably consistent despite dealing with major injuries, including the lengthy absence of Aaron Judge . They entered Sunday's game with an 85-63 record and had won 19 of their previous 30 games. They then beat the Mets 2-0 behind another dominant performance from Cam Schlittler .

Yes, the Yankees may not be the favorite.

But they are becoming increasingly difficult to dismiss.

Yankees Have Enough Offense and Pitching to Win It All

The most encouraging part of the Yankees' season may be that they haven't needed one player to carry them every night.

Giancarlo Stanton has been limited, and Judge missed 85 games with a fractured rib. Yet New York has continued to produce. The Yankees have scored 677 runs through 149 games, averaging 4.54 runs per game, while hitting 202 home runs.

That isn't an overwhelming offensive attack by Yankees standards.

Cody Bellinger has provided a .777 OPS, while Jorge Polanco has been one of the team's better offensive performers. Even with Judge's extended absence, the Yankees have found enough production throughout the lineup to remain one of the American League's best teams.

His numbers since returning haven't been spectacular, but simply having the reigning superstar available for the postseason changes the equation. He went 3-for-14 in his first four games back, but manager Aaron Boone has been encouraged by his swing decisions and timing.

That might ultimately be what gives the Yankees their best chance.

Cam Schlittler has emerged as a legitimate ace. The righty entered Sunday's game with a 13-6 record and 2.01 ERA before throwing six innings of one-hit ball against the Mets . He struck out nine and lowered his league-leading ERA to 1.95.

Gerrit Cole has also provided quality innings since returning from Tommy John surgery, although his recent struggles against the Mets demonstrate that he isn't invincible.

The Yankees don't need perfect pitching. They need good pitching, timely hitting and Judge healthy.

They have a legitimate chance of getting all three.

Dodgers Are Still the Team to Beat, But Yanks Have a Chance

It would be foolish to pretend the Dodgers suddenly aren't the favorites.

They have won two straight World Series and entered September looking like the most complete team in baseball. Even after Sunday's 6-4 loss to Miami , Los Angeles is still 90-59 and remains in excellent position heading into the postseason.

But there are reasons to think this postseason could be different.

The Dodgers placed their superstar on the injured list because of left knee and right biceps issues, with the move designed to give him time to recover before the postseason. Ohtani has still produced 30 home runs and 80 RBIs while posting a 1.79 ERA in his limited pitching work, but he hasn't pitched since July and is not expected to return to the mound this season.

The Dodgers can still win without Ohtani pitching. They can probably win without him for stretches offensively.

But asking them to win another championship without their biggest weapon at full strength is a different proposition.

New York has survived injuries, maintained a winning pace and developed a potential postseason ace in Schlittler. If Judge is healthy and the rest of the lineup continues producing, the Yankees have enough offense to challenge anyone.

The last time the Yankees won the World Series was 2009.

The Dodgers are still the frontrunners to win it all again.

But at +700, with 40% of this week's wagers coming their way, the Yankees are clearly becoming the team bettors believe can stop them.

And maybe that is the most important development of all.

articles.title: Miracle League of Arkansas celebrates 20th season in Little Rock
articles.summary: LITTLE ROCK, Ark. — From players stepping up to the plate to families cheering from the sidelines, there was plenty of excitement Saturday as Miracle League...
articles.body:
LITTLE ROCK, Ark. — From players stepping up to the plate to families cheering from the sidelines, there was plenty of excitement Saturday as Miracle League of Arkansas kicked off its 20th season.

The league gives children and adults with disabilities the opportunity to play baseball in an inclusive environment designed to meet their needs.

For families like the Elams, the chance to see their child take the field means even more.

"The joy of getting to watch our kid be included in a sport ... we've always wanted him to be able to do something athletic and be able to be a part of a team," said Alex Elam, whose son Jensen plays in the league. "Getting to watch him be a part of a team is fantastic."

Jensen is blind, but that has not stopped him from finding ways to be part of the game.

"It makes me feel like a proud dad," Jensen's father, Michael Elam, said. "I've always dreamed of him playing ... in my mind would be a normal sport, but he gets to do all kinds of things that I didn't realize were even possible."

Peggy McCall, who founded Miracle League of Arkansas, said the league has given families countless moments worth celebrating over the past 20 years.

"We celebrate the big stuff, but I think we celebrate the little things even more because it takes so long sometimes," McCall-Robertson said.

More than 3,000 athletes have taken the field through Miracle League of Arkansas programs over the past two decades.

But McCall said the impact of the league goes beyond baseball.

Players often remain on the same teams for years, giving them the opportunity to build friendships and a sense of community, she said.

"The players, they get on a team and often they stay for a while, and so they build ... they have a team and they have teammates, and they have their own community," McCall said. "As they get older and have phones, they're talking to each other and doing things outside of the ballpark. It's the best thing ever."

That sense of community extends to the families, too.

"It's so much fun to be able to connect with other families that are also going through the same thing," Alex Elam said. "Being able to all watch them, all the kids be so excited about getting to hit a ball and watch the parents be happy about it too, that's just an absolute blessing."

Opening Day also brought food, fellowship and volunteers to Miracle League Little Rock Field. First Community Bank grilled hot dogs and burgers as players, families and supporters gathered to celebrate the start of the anniversary season.

After 20 years, the league is continuing its mission of making sure everyone who wants to play has the opportunity to take the field.

And while the new season is underway, Jensen has one request — cooler weather.

"It's gotta change," Jensen said. "And if it doesn't I will faint." McCall says the league is always looking for more volunteers to sign up on their website .

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese’s locker room celebration with Team USA after World Cup win goes viral

Team USA celebrated its 2026 FIBA World Cup win in the locker room after defeating France 97-79 in the final.

Team USA's 20-year undefeated streak at the FIBA World Cup gets even longer as the national team asserts its dominance in international basketball once again.

Angel Reese gets Caitlin Clark to make a TikTok alongside Team USA teammates

Reese shared a video of the entire team celebrating their gold medals in the locker room, which also features Clark performing a champagne shower on her teammates.

While Clark is active on her own Instagram when it comes to making occasional posts and stories, she is not known to indulge in making short-form video for Reels or TikTok.

Many WNBA stars are very active on TikTok and other platforms, so getting Clark to feature in one is quite rare since we have not seen Clark feature in videos with other WNBA players.

Reese and Clark have been two of the biggest talking points of the tournament as the future of the national team, especially with their strong on-court connection.

Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese left an impact on the court

Reese averaged 7.2 points on 59.1% from the field and 5.0 rebounds over six games at the World Cup. Clark averaged 7.8 points on 35.9% from the field but led the national team in assists with 5.3 per game.

Neither played a big role in the final, as Clark scored 12 points on five shots with three assists in 13 minutes of action. Reese played just nine minutes, scoring three points and grabbing three rebounds.

Their on-court connection was clear to see, with Clark assisting Reese multiple times with picture-perfect passes that had fans dreaming of the rivals eventually teaming up in the WNBA.

With Clark emphatically letting reporters know that she and Reese have been friends behind-the-scenes of their on-court rivalry, it can't be ruled out that the star duo eventually considers teaming up.
