articles.title: Rutgers Football Opens as 25.5 Point Underdogs vs No.12 USC
articles.summary: Will Rutgers cover the 24.5 point spread?
articles.body:
After falling 37-21 to UMass in week one and losing 28-21 to Boston College on the road in week two, Rutgers football opened as a 25.5-point underdog against No.12 USC before the line quickly moved to listing the Scarlet Knights as a 24.5-point underdog per FanDuel . The total over/under in this game is listed at 58.5 points.

This game has the potential to get very ugly very quickly for Rutgers, who has been plagued by inconsistent quarterback, offensive line, and defensive play over the past two games. In the first three weeks of the season, the Trojans trounced their weak non-conference schedule, handing blowout losses to Louisiana , Fresno State and San Diego State . Their game against the Knights will be their first taste of Power Four play this year.

In their most recent game against the Rajin Cajuns, USC quarterback Jayden Maiava threw for 261 yards and five touchdowns. Rutgers is still trying to figure out who the best quarterback on the roster is, as both Dylan Lonergan and AJ Surace threw more interceptions than touchdowns in the games they have played.

USC running back King Miller totaled 28 carries for 128 yards and one touchdown last game, while Mark Bowman was their leading receiver with 6 catches for 83 yards and two touchdowns.

Strangely enough, the Trojans' defense hasn't looked its best early on this season, surrendering 30 points to Louisiana and 26 points to San Diego State, two teams they should reasonably keep near a shutout. Both teams have quarterbacks who led them in both passing yards and rushing yards. Rutgers doesn't have a typical mobile quarterback, meaning that they won't likely be able to exploit this to get some sort of offense going.

With the recent performance of both teams, it is really hard to see Rutgers covering the spread. Had the results of the first two games been drastically different, it would have been much easier to see, but now that the season seems to be in a free fall, it just looks out of reach. USC has scored at least 39 points in their last three matchups, meaning that when their offense gets rolling, they are likely going to the game on a track meet that Rutgers' offense doesn't have the ability to keep up with, or the defense to slow down.

Rutgers will kick off against USC inside SHI Stadium on Saturday, September 19 at 3:30 p.m. The game will be broadcast live on CBS.

articles.title: Xander Bogaerts can be better than this
articles.summary: Padres shortstop having his worst season.
articles.body:
During his time as the control partner of the San Diego Padres , the late Peter Seidler was aggressive with spending money to build a core of players for the team he loved. Signing Manny Machado to a long-term contract and then extending him when he had an opt-out option, Seidler committed a total of $470 million to Machado for his contract covering 2019 through 2033.

When Seidler and general manager A.J. Preller recognized the exciting talent of the Padres' young shortstop, Fernando Tatis Jr., they negotiated a 14-year contract extension that committed him to the Padres through 2034 and pays $340 million.

Infielder Jake Cronenworth, the Padres defensive specialist at multiple positions, was given a much smaller contract at seven years and $80 million to anchor the infield while being able to play all four infield spots. Cronenworth's contract presently looks to be a bargain for a player that will never be a superstar but is steady and reliable while playing excellent defense at multiple spots.

The team will likely believe that all of those contracts were justified in the long run. Even Machado, who is on a Hall-of-Fame career track, was a defensible decision based on his contract being the one that established the organization as being serious about contending and his standing as the team's leader on and off the field.

The head scratcher, the player signed to a contract that seemed a massive overpay at the time and even more so now, is shortstop Xander Bogaerts. There is no denying he was a superstar in his time with the Boston Red Sox , earning multiple World Series championships. When his contract ended with Boston, the Padres outbid everyone else in the running. The Red Sox infamously offered Bogaerts a 4-year, $90 million contract, then upped it to six years and $160 million. The Cubs were rumored to have offered him a multi-year, $200 million contract.

The Padres blew all those offers out of the water, signing Bogaerts, 30-years-old at the time, to an 11-year, $280 million deal that carried through the 2033 season, when Bogaerts will be 41 years old.

It was a puzzling decision by Seidler and the Padres. They already had multiple shortstops on the roster with Tatis being a blooming superstar. In his first year with the Padres, Bogaerts hit a respectable .285/.350/.440 with 19 home runs and 58 RBI. That 2023 season was his best as a Padre.

Since the 2023 season, Bogaerts has declined offensively each year. Some of that can be attributed to injuries, with a broken shoulder and broken foot affecting his 2024 and 2025 seasons.

So far in 2026, Xander Bogaerts has been relatively healthy. With a hamstring scare and a ball fouled off his foot in August, Bogaerts left those games but was never held from a game or placed on the injured list. Despite having no significant injury this season, Bogaerts is having his worst season as an MLB player. At 33-years-old, Bogaerts is at the back end of his peak production as a professional player. A players' peak years are considered to be between the age of 27 and 32 with production tailing significantly after that age.

With seven years remaining on his contract, Bogaerts is in the declining years of his career. With a look at his stats, it appears his hitting is the first to go.

Bogaerts started the season strong in 2026. In April, he hit .292/.382/.472 with five home runs and 15 RBI. He had a good spring, hitting .286 with a .819 OPS, so his strong start was very encouraging. Unfortunately, May brought expectations back down to earth. Hitting .204 in May and .211 in June, Bogaerts managed just six extra-base hits in 51 games.

July was even worse, hitting .167 with a .523 OPS in 24 games. In 27 games in August, Bogaerts hit .212 with a .674 OPS, with seven extra-base hits and 11 RBI.

For September's 10 games, Bogaerts is pushing his numbers up as the team is making a playoff push. Hitting .314/.415/.371 with a .786 OPS, Bogaerts is following a trend in his career of improving his numbers during the last month of the season.

If there is one silver lining to the Bogaerts situation, it is his defense at shortstop. After switching him to second base for 85 games in 2024 to accommodate Ha-Seong Kim at shortstop, Bogaerts has been their primary shortstop. From 2023 through this season, Bogaerts has been in the 80th percentile or above in Outs Above Average as a shortstop. In 2025, he finished in the 93rd percentile with seven OAA. He has improved his arm strength during his time with the Padres, even though it continues to be below average.

It seems unlikely that a drastic improvement in his offense will occur at this point in his career. Bogaerts, an admired leader on the team, will need to work over the next offseason to evaluate what needs to change. Looking at his Baseball Savant page, Bogaerts has not lost bat speed or exit velocity over his time with the Padres. He does not strike out more or chase more than in past years. At best, his stats portray an average to below-average major league hitter. That is borne out in his status as the No. 8 hitter in the Padres lineup, a spot unfamiliar to a player with Bogaerts' past pedigree.

Machado made swing changes this past offseason in order to improve his bat speed and exit velocity, he has not recovered from the slump those changes threw him into. He is also having the worst year of his career in batting average numbers. Machado is still the best power hitter on the team and leads in RBI, but players need to show caution when reworking their swings as they age.

Bogaerts can still be a valuable player for the Padres if he can improve his offense to average. His underlying numbers indicate he still can do that. Bogaerts will have to make the adjustments all aging players must make.

It is too late to live up to the contract he signed. Both Bogaerts and Machado will long be done as players before the Padres stop paying them. What Bogaerts needs to focus on is adjusting his game so he can be a contributor for as long as possible.

articles.title: Cowboys mistakes and missed opportunities doom them in opener
articles.summary: Cowboys drop their season opener to the New York Giants
articles.body:
In the immediate aftermath of the loss, one thing is exceptionally clear: the Dallas Cowboys left far too many plays on the field. From penalties to missed opportunities, Dallas was outplayed by both the New York Giants and themselves.

Dallas had seven penalties for 60 yards in just the first half alone. They would end up finishing the game with nine penalties for 90 yards. This included a taunting call from Javonte Williams late into the fourth quarter en route to a touchdown, leading to a missed PAT.

Paired with that, the Cowboys defense finished with five turnover-worthy plays but only walked away with a single takeaway. From forced fumbles that just bounced the wrong way to dropped interceptions, the Cowboys defense just couldn't take advantage. On a night where the Giants moved the ball slowly yet methodically down the field, chewing up clock on the way to the endzone, this defense needed to finish when the ball was up for grabs. They just didn't do that.

As mentioned earlier in the week , one of the ways that Dallas could lose this game was due to lack of defensive scheme experience and familiarity. This lack of experience certainly factored into the large voids left on the field by Cowboys defenders leading to multiple New York Giants touchdowns. These mistakes allowed the Giants offense to convert on third downs at a rate of 81%. This kept the Cowboys offense off the field for much of the second half.

And let's not give the offense a pass. Against the Giants, George Pickens was not the same player that we saw throughout training camp. Two untimely drops resulted in a punt and an eventual turnover – an interception thrown by Dak just before the half on a ball he seemingly meant to throw away. The Giants would go and score back-to-back touchdowns after that mistake and never look back. The dropped deep ball from Pickens was a turning point in this game.

The expectation for the Cowboys was to come into their division rivals house and knock them down. But Dallas found out the hard way that when you play an underdog like the Giants in their own stadium, the quickest way to lose is to commit untimely penalties, turn the ball over, and miss your opportunities at big plays. The Cowboys did just that, and now they will start the season 0-1.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts Gets Honest on His Place in Eagles Offense After Commanders Win
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is just a year removed from a Super Bowl victory. But for a lot of pundits, Hurts has quite a bit to prove this s...
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is just a year removed from a Super Bowl victory. But for a lot of pundits, Hurts has quite a bit to prove this season.

Hurts came into the regular season one the most scrutinized signal-callers around the league. Yet, he's trying to adapt to a new play-caller while replacing his top outside target in A.J. Brown .

With that in mind, there are going to be growing pains. It's undeniable. But when he has to, Hurts can still fall back on his raw athletic ability. It's just a matter of the quarterback recognizing the right time to do that versus when he should stay within his new offense.

Hurts discussed that difficult tightrope after beating the Commanders in Week 1.

"Yeah," Hurts said after a long pause to a question about whether he feels it's necessary to "take over" the offense sometimes. "But it's not something that's forced. It's the same focus that you have throughout the whole entire game. It's the same poise that you play with throughout the whole entire game.

"It goes back to all 11 being on the same page and then me taking responsibility with the opportunities that I have with the ball in my hand."

The best example of that from Week 1 was Hurts scrambling for a 22-yard gain on third-and-18 during the fourth quarter. The conversion enabled the Eagles to continue a drive that eventually ended with a 43-yard touchdown pass.

That touchdown held up as the game-winning score in the 24-22 victory.

Eagles' Jalen Hurts Gives Candid Answer on Feeling When to 'Take Over'

Hurts is so athletic with his legs that it would be easy for him to feel as though he should "take over" on nearly every play, especially broken ones. Before last season, Hurts had rushed for at least 600 yards in four consecutive campaigns.

And even last season, Hurts posted 421 rushing yards with eight touchdowns.

But the Eagles quarterback understands that the scramble drill isn't going to work consistently. And the more he does it, the fewer game repetitions his fellow offensive playmakers will have running the plays Sean Mannion calls for them.

Then again, when the game is on the line, Hurts and the Eagles shouldn't think twice if the quarterback using his legs is the best way to move the chains.

That's what happened with about eight minutes left in the fourth quarter on third and very long.

Hurts' scramble could have been the difference in the game. Three plays after the run, the Eagles moved back ahead by eight points. Philadelphia held on to win after stopping Washington's 2-point conversion attempt.

articles.title: Was Montreal Canadiens’ Nick Suzuki Snubbed in NHL’s Latest Rankings?
articles.summary: Captain Nick Suzuki led the Montreal Canadiens throughout the 2025-26 season.Considering his ongoing impact on the franchise, it’s no surprise that the NHL r...
articles.body:
Captain Nick Suzuki led the Montreal Canadiens throughout the 2025-26 season.

Considering his ongoing impact on the franchise, it's no surprise that the NHL ranked him among its top 30 players this season.

But he ranked rather low on the final list — was he snubbed?

Where Montreal Canadiens' Nick Suzuki Ranked Among the NHL's Elite

In small increments, NHL.com will release its rankings of the top 30 players across the league.

His 2026-27 campaign will mark his eighth season in the NHL, with each year spent in Montreal.

Last year, the 27-year-old center skated in 82 games and scored 29 goals with 72 assists for 101 points.

He ranked sixth among skaters in all of hockey with his 101 points, trailing Mark Scheifele (103), Macklin Celebrini (115), Nathan MacKinnon (127), Nikita Kucherov (130) and Connor McDavid (138).

He also became the fifth player in franchise history to reach 100 points in a single season and the first to do so in four decades.

Specifically looking at the Canadiens, Suzuki led the team in games played, ranked third in goals, first in assists and first in points.

Simply looking at his consistent, massive impact on the franchise, he looks to have been snubbed.

But let's not forget that the NHL's rankings include the league's top players, including veterans McDavid, MacKinnon, Kucherov and 29 others.

Suzuki was selected 13th overall in the first round of the 2017 NHL draft.

In September 2018, the Vegas Golden Knights traded him to Montreal in exchange for Max Pacioretty . He's remained with the franchise since.

In October 2021, he signed an eight-year, $63 million contract extension with the Canadiens. This deal runs through the 2029-30 season.

As he stated upon signing, per NHL.com , "I love the city of Montreal. I love being a Canadien, and to do that for hopefully the next nine years is something I'm really looking forward to. It's huge for me and my family and we're really happy that it all worked out."

Suzuki is originally from London, Ontario, Canada, which made this signing all the more special.

He has made a valuable addition to Montreal's team — continuing to meet that bar will be imperative for their success during their 2026-27 campaign.

articles.body:
Well, that didn't go according to the Cowboys ' plans.

After an offseason that featured a complete overhaul of the Dallas defense, led by new defensive coordinator Christian Parker and a host of new pieces on that side of the ball, the Cowboys offered little resistance to Jaxson Dart and the New York Giants in a 28-20 season-opening loss .

While the Giants' offensive numbers weren't overly gaudy, they were able to move the chains all evening and bleed the clock to the point that Dallas' offense only had two possessions in the second half. New York racked up 29 first downs, 394 yards and converted 9 of 11 third downs.

There was plenty of hope in Dallas throughout training camp and a definitive buzz that Parker had the Cowboys' defense back on track after a dismal 2025 season. Unfortunately for Parker, his debut as the Dallas defensive coordinator was reminiscent of last year's unit under Eberflus.

It's safe to say Cowboys fans and NFL media alike were harsh on the Dallas defense after Sunday night's performance.

articles.title: Ex-Eagles LB Sounds Off On Jalen Hurts Critic After Commanders Win
articles.summary: Entering the first week of the 2026 NFL season, the Philadelphia Eagles’ offense was getting put to the test. After firing the former offensive coordinator K...
articles.body:
Entering the first week of the 2026 NFL season, the Philadelphia Eagles ' offense was getting put to the test.

After firing the former offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo at the end of the Eagles' 2025 playoff run, the team hired Sean Mannion to take over.

The performance of the unit as a whole didn't exactly wow the viewers. When it comes to Jalen Hurts ' performance, the well-known analyst Colin Cowherd took a shot at the 2024 Super Bowl MVP. The former linebacker, Emmanuel Acho , quickly came to Hurts' defense.

"Eagles have four 3 & Outs. That's with a top OLine, Saquon, and solid WR/TE talent. Not sure how much more you can give Jalen Hurts," Cowherd wrote on X.

"Don't dare blame Jalen Hurts. He's the only reason the Eagles won," Acho wrote in response to Cowherd .

"Just turn on the game tape and take a look and Landon Dickerson and this 'top OLine'."

It's true that two seasons ago, the Eagles employed one of the NFL's finest offensive lines. They have plenty of star power up front, and Hurts managed to find a lot of time to scan the field and let them rip.

Last season turned out to be a different story. Names like Jordan Mailata , Cam Jurgens , and Landon Dickerson struggled as they played through injuries. The All-Pro Lane Johnson missed a chunk of time due to setbacks.

Sunday's action against the Washington Commanders didn't look much better for the Eagles' offensive line. Still, Hurts managed to utilize his athleticism to the fullest and willed the Eagles to a win.

Hurts threw 25 passes against the Commanders, completing 14 of his attempts. He tossed for three touchdowns and didn't turn the ball over at all. He posted a 122.2 passer rating.

Beyond his passing, Hurts used his legs, which was a common concern about his game last season. He kept the ball on the ground for seven rushes, going for 46 yards. He had a clutch 22-yard run in the fourth quarter.

The Eagles came out on top with a 24-22 victory. It might not have been the strongest offensive showing, but Hurts was far from the problem.

articles.title: Devils beaten by Blaze comeback in Challenge Cup
articles.summary: Cardiff Devils twice let slip a one goal lead as they were beaten 3-2 at Coventry Blaze in the Challenge Cup at the Skydome Arena.
articles.body:
Cardiff Devils twice let slip a one goal lead as they were beaten 3-2 at Coventry Blaze in the Challenge Cup at the Skydome Arena.

Carson Musser scored the winner with just over four minutes left for Blaze, who had suffered a 6-0 opening game defeat by Sheffield Steelers 24 hours earlier.

Cardiff - who had begun their campaign with a 3-1 win over Guildford Flames - opened the scoring through Bayley Harewood.

It was a first Elite League goal for Barry-born Harewood, playing in his first full-time season for Devils.

The first period ended 1-1 after Griffin Ness' leveller, only for Kohen Olischefski to restore the Welsh side's lead in a second period that also saw them lose forward Riley Brandt to a major penalty.

Ryan Richardson brought the home side level again with a power-play goal midway through the third, before Musser secured the comeback win.

"Those were tough conditions; the ice was terrible. It didn't sit down all night, and it's hard to play your game, but that's for both teams," said Devils' head coach Paul Thompson.

"In this game you have got to take your chances when they come along. We didn't get that 3-1 goal, which may have sealed it. Credit to the Blaze for coming back."

Sheffield Steelers top the Group A table after the opening weekend, having followed up their handsome opening victory against Blaze with a shoot-out win at Guildford.

Nottingham Panthers are second, despite their game at Manchester Storm being called off, with Blaze third and Devils in fourth place.

Storm - who are due to host Cardiff on Friday, 18 September - were unable to play the game because of "technical issues with the ice" at the AO arena.

articles.title: “Our Greatest Motivation Is Playing for Chivas and Winning” – Gabriel Milito
articles.summary: The 3-0 win over Pumas left Guadalajara with plenty of positive takeaways in Apertura 2026, as the result temporarily moved the Rebaño into first place in th...
articles.body:
The 3-0 win over Pumas left Guadalajara with plenty of positive takeaways in Apertura 2026, as the result temporarily moved the Rebaño into first place in the standings. However, for Gabriel Milito , there is no greater motivation than playing for Chivas and always looking for the win, regardless of who stands in their way.

Following Rebaño 's emphatic performance tonight at Estadio AKRON , the Rojiblanco head coach spoke to the media and highlighted his team's performance, their clinical finishing, and the collective work they put in every match. The Rojiblanco boss also discussed the outstanding form of Santiago Sandoval and Hugo Camberos , as well as Roberto Alvarado 's leadership on the pitch.

Gabriel Milito's Words at the Press Conference

"For us, the greatest motivation is winning."Our commitment is to ourselves: to play well, compete to the best of our abilities, and put ourselves in the best possible position to win."Our greatest motivation is playing for Chivas, regardless of who we're facing."

Satisfaction With the Win and the Team's Performance

"We're happy with the win and with the team's performance. We had a good opponent in front of us, with great players."I'm satisfied with the performance of the entire team, from start to finish."

A Match That Reflected the Team's Playing Style

"We were clinical throughout the match, controlled the game with the ball, and knew how to organize ourselves when they had possession to prevent a counterattack. That's how we want to play."We give it the value it deserves when you put in a great performance. We always try to play this way. Today we played very well, and we have to keep moving in this direction."

Santiago Sandoval and His Outstanding Form

"We've known Sando since the day we arrived, and I've always said it: he's a difference-maker, a player with an eye for goal. He has tremendous potential and is going through a great moment. The challenge now is maintaining it. I'm happy for him."

The Clásico and the Importance of Every Match

"The Clásico is the most important match in Mexico , but for us, every game is extremely important because the first thing we want is to represent Chivas very well, regardless of the opponent."Obviously, because of everything surrounding the match, it will be a different week, but in terms of our commitment, we'll prepare for it just like every other match we have to play."

Santi and Camberos With Their Sights Set on the National Team

"As for Santi and Camberos, if they're being watched by the national team today, it's because of their outstanding performances. We have to handle it calmly and with a lot of humility. We're here to guide them, and we won't allow them to lose perspective. Above all, humility."

Roberto Alvarado, an Example On and Off the Pitch

"Roberto Alvarado is a star both on and off the pitch. We all enjoy having him around; he's a player who plays with a lot of heart. If there's an example to follow, it's 'Piojo.' For us, having him is a blessing. He not only gives us performances, but he's also an example to follow."

articles.title: Davey reignites international ambitions with Wales
articles.summary: Uncapped Wales scrum-half Megan Davey's admits she almost called it quits before her recent call-up at the age of 26.
articles.body:
Megan Davey's international ambitions have been reignited at her self-proclaimed 'old' age of 26.

Loughborough Lightning's record appearance holder considered going into full-time teaching when she did not make Wales' 2026 Six Nations squad.

Her hopes were dashed again when omitted from Sean Lynn's extended training squad for the WXV Global Series.

"There was a little bit of a wobble," admitted uncapped Davey.

"It's hard to keep going when you're at my age, you feel old in the game."

"There's always been something inside me, I know I can do it, it's the voice inside my head that's kept me going," she said.

"I was really happy that I got an opportunity."

Davey qualifies for Wales through her grandfather from Llanelli but went through the English pathway system as a youngster.

"The avenue for under-20s was always really with England because it wasn't as set up with Wales, but now it's really good," she said.

"I'm a little bit older...now I feel like I can really do people proud."

And despite being a latecomer in camp, Davey says everyone has been welcoming.

"There's always that thing when you walk into an environment that's already established, you're like 'how am I going to do?' but I was really raring to go," she added.

"Obviously a bit sad that I wasn't in the squad to begin with, but you just crack on with what you're doing."

Davey has primarily trained at scrum-half with Wales and faces competition from Keira Bevan and Seren Lockwood.

And contrary to the stereotype of the position, the nines get along with no animosity.

"We all really enjoy each other's company. We want each other to do well, so there's never that hatred towards each other," said Davey, who has previously started at fly-half for Loughborough.

"Whoever goes out there and does the job first is the best pick for the team and you just need to back that completely."

Wales open their WXV campaign against South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park on Friday, 18 September (19:15 BST), and any potential involvement would mean the world to Davey.

"Playing international rugby is such a privilege and I want to make everyone proud - my family, but also the coaches that have been behind me for the last 15 years of my journey," she said.

"It's just that final step, like 'I made it'. I'm really excited and hopefully it comes at some point."

If it weren't for the New York Knicks , the city of New York would be in shambles from a sporting point of view. Their football situation, in particular, looked bleak. After all, the New York Giants and New York Jets combined for just seven wins out of 34 games last season.

But with the new NFL season being upon us, hope is renewed for the people of New York — if the Knicks can break their 53-year championship drought, why can't their football teams shock the world in similar fashion as well?

On Sunday, the Giants kicked off their 2026 season with a 28-20 win over division rival Dallas Cowboys at home. During this game at MetLife Stadium, a hero during the Knicks' title run, Jose Alvarado , was in attendance. As one would expect, Alvarado got quite the warm reception from the fans in attendance — with the Knicks guard hyping up the crowd when he was introduced.

The spirits remain high in New York city, and the Knicks have certainly rallied a city that's been crying out for success in sports. Of course, the New York Liberty did win the WNBA championship in 2024, so it's not like the city has been in a long title-winning drought. But this is the Big Apple, where expectations are high, year-in, year-out.

Alvarado played a huge role in the Knicks' comeback victory in Game 4 of the 2026 NBA Finals against the San Antonio Spurs . He was on the court for the final few minutes of that contest, igniting a spark that spurred New York to a historic comeback victory from 29 points down .

The 28-year-old guard from Puerto Rico endeared himself to the Knicks fanbase rather quickly, and he's expected to provide a boost off the bench this year once more while backing up the King of New York himself, Jalen Brunson .

articles.title: South Korean officials decry ‘worst ever’ Asian Games accommodation
articles.summary: Organisers in Japan say they had ‘neither the manpower nor the budget’ to deal with the accommodation shortage.
articles.body:
Accommodation at the Asian Games, which start this week in Japan, is the “worst ever”, say South Korean officials, warning of “a serious shortage” of rooms.

Beds in shipping container-style huts are too short for players to stretch out, the South Korean basketball chief said on Monday, while officials from the Philippines resorted to Airbnb.

There is no dedicated athletes’ village for the games, with organisers instead relying on a cruise ship, temporary wooden cabins and hotels to cut costs.

The games in the city of Nagoya in Aichi prefecture officially open on Saturday, but football and basketball are already under way.

Jung Jae-yong, vice president of the Korea Basketball Association (KBA), expressed his displeasure with the cabins where the men’s basketball team is staying.

“Based on my experience, this is the worst it has ever been,” he said.

“Athletes who are over two metres tall cannot even stretch their legs out on the beds. It’s unreasonable.”

Byeon Jun-hyeong, from the basketball team, posted a video on social media showing a leaking sink and a soaked floor in his hut.

The huts are set to be home to 2,000 athletes and officials over the more than two weeks of the games.

Worried about their athletes, Indian sports officials built replicas of cabins to help them get used to the games’ accommodation.

KBA’s Jung accused organisers of failing to respond to South Korea’s concerns.

“The organisers have still not said anything,” he said.

“We are very concerned and discussing extensively with the Korean Sport and Olympic Committee what to do about this.”

Hundreds of athletes were briefly evacuated from their accommodation last week as record rainfall lashed Nagoya.

More rain has been forecast in the coming days.

More than 17,000 athletes and officials are expected at the games — a bigger number than the Olympics.

Organisers were initially expecting 15,000 and argued last month that they had “neither the manpower nor the budget” to deal with ballooning numbers.

The Olympic Council of Asia later said everyone would get a place to stay.

Star cricketers have voiced fears about a lack of top-notch hotels.

A Korean Sport & Olympic Committee (KSOC) official agreed that problems persist with the games just days away.

“At the moment, there is a serious shortage of accommodation not only for the entire South Korean delegation to the Asian Games, but for delegations from around the world in the Aichi-Nagoya area,” the official said.

“We are doing everything we can to resolve the issue and ensure there are no such problems.”

Philippine Olympic Committee president Abraham Tolentino said all athletes from his country had been given a room. However, “some officials, like coaches, were moved to different hotels and Airbnb”.

The Italian cruise ship Costa Serena is due to arrive in Nagoya on Tuesday. Between 4,000 and 5,000 athletes will stay on the vessel.

The rest will be accommodated in hotels, including in Tokyo, where swimming, diving and equestrian events will take place.

articles.title: El Grande Americano, Omos, Real Winners and Losers of WWE's AAA Triplemanía 34 Weekend
articles.summary: At a time when WWE's main roster product is more polarizing than ever before, AAA is generating genuine buzz with strong shows, simple stories and memorable matches and moments.
articles.body:
At a time when WWE's main roster product is more polarizing than ever before, AAA is generating genuine buzz with strong shows, simple stories and memorable matches and moments.

Triplemania 34 weekend was crucial in ensuring AAA established itself as a much-needed alternative to Raw and SmackDown while still being under the WWE umbrella. Ultimately, the event delivered in spades.

Night 1 was largely average on the whole but featured its fair share of entertaining action, headlined by a brief yet brutal bout between Rey Mysterio and Omos. It was easily outshined by Night 2 thanks to the three title changes and an outstanding main event.

The electric atmosphere in Mexico City alone made Night 2 feel like AAA's biggest event of the year and offered enough of an incentive for fans unfamiliar with what the brand's been doing to tune in going forward.

From El Grande Americano to The War Raiders, these are the real winners and losers of WWE's Triplemania 34 weekend.

Triple H was quick to cast Omos to the side immediately upon usurping Vince McMahon as the head of WWE's creative direction in the summer of 2022. Omos' role on WWE TV was drastically curtailed over the year that followed before he was pulled from programming entirely.

It wasn't until he resurfaced in AAA a year ago that he started making waves again by winning the annual Copa Bardahl match and aligning himself with El Hijo del Vikingo. Vikingo's injury earlier this year paved the way for him to join forces with reigning AAA Mega champion Dominik Mysterio instead.

Omos had himself an incredible weekend by first knocking off Rey Mysterio in the main event of Night 1 of Triplemania 34 (including brutalizing the WWE Hall of Famer while strapped to a stretcher afterward) and then winning the Copa Bardahl matchup for the second straight year on Night 2.

He also interfered in the AAA Mega Championship main event but was thwarted by El Grande Americano.

The powers that be at AAA have utilized Omos exceptionally well as a monster heel and have portrayed him as the ultimate obstacle. His stock has skyrocketed coming out of Triplemania, potentially putting him in contention for the AAA Mega title sooner rather than later.

Roxanne Perez hasn't won a match that has mattered on WWE TV all year, yet she has come across like an absolute star any time she's appeared in AAA.

On Night 1 of Triplemania 34, Perez participated in a Fatal 4-Way to determine La Catalina's AAA Reina de Reinas Championship challenger at Worlds Collide on Sept. 26. She won the bout by pinning La Heidra.

Perez's above-average in-ring ability has never been called into question, but her booking has certainly been questionable for a great while. The Judgment Day undoubtedly helped her land a recurring role on Raw upon her arrival on the brand last year, but the group has done more to hold her back than elevate her to that next level in 2026.

Challenging for and potentially winning the Reina de Reinas title won't automatically make her a top talent on Raw, but her newfound push on the brand has reminded fans of what she's capable of and has encouraged the conversation of WWE doing more with her on Monday nights.

Money in the Bank is right around the corner, and whether she's wearing AAA gold by then or not, it would be booking malpractice for her not to be involved in that high-stakes Ladder match, let alone win the whole thing.

It wasn't a great weekend for The Psycho Circus and specifically Psycho Clown, who not only lost the AAA World Trios Championship on Night 1 but also a Mexican Street Fight to El Carnicero on Night 2.

Carnicero cost Psycho Circus the Trios titles on Friday night, which effectively built toward the Mexican Street Fight on Sunday night. It was a hard-hitting war between the two before Pagano got involved, betrayed Clown by revealing an alliance with Carnicero, and aiding Carnicero to victory.

Clown will now have quite a bit to avenge going forward between attempting to regain the Trios titles and settling his score with Pagano and Carnicero. Presumably, that will involve him and the rest of Psycho Circus battling Pagano and Carnicero in tag team action, possibly on a number of occasions.

Although Clown has been a staple of AAA since WWE took control of the company in early 2026, his booking at Triplemania indicated that he won't be someone the brand is built around going forward. He's popular enough and can excel in extreme environments but has yet to be presented as anything other than a stepping stone.

It was the tale of two tag team matches at Triplemania 34, with one coming close to stealing the weekend while the other fell flat despite actually having something at stake.

Night 1 featured Fatal 4-Way action with Los Americanos, Fraxiom, The Tokyo Boys and The LWO producing an incredible, fast-paced encounter. Nothing was on the line, but it did serve as a showcase for the four tandems and reminded fans of just how exciting tag team wrestling can be.

It was a much different story on Night 2 when Galeno and El Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr. answered The War Raiders' open challenge and beat them in fairly forgettable match to clinch the AAA World Tag Team Championship.

The Raiders were fresh off a successful title defense on Friday's SmackDown against Damian Priest and R-Truth. They weren't in possession of the twin titles for very long and it's clear holding them did very little to reaffirm their dominance.

AAA borrowing talented teams from Raw and SmackDown to fill out its tag division is completely fine, but there needs to be more emphasis on making those titles matter. Galeno and Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr. might restore some interest with their reign, but only if they're afforded the opportunity to do so.

Previous iterations of Los Perros del Mal ran roughshod over AAA on and off for decades, so the decision to bring them back—albeit with new members—was a wise one.

After gradually building momentum for months and orchestrating attacks on the entire roster, the group made a major statement at Triplemania 34 by besting The Psycho Circus on Night 1 to win the AAA World Trios Championship.

Los Garza, Daga and Karmen Petrovic came back out on Night 2 in the wake of the AAA World Cruiserweight Championship match to lay waste to Rey Fenix, Jack Cartwheel, Nathan Frazer and Mini Vikingo in emphatic fashion.

The reaction they received in Mexico City and cemented their status as stars, as if it wasn't already obvious prior to the event.

They're a force to be reckoned with in AAA and now have the hardware to back it up. It remains to be seen who will step up and pose a legitimate threat to them, but until then, may their reign of terror continue.

El Grande Americano was the uncrowned champion of AAA going into Triplemania 34 and now he can finally call himself the company ace.

His Night 2 main event with Dominik Mysterio had been built up over many months and managed to capture a big fight feel. While not as epic as Americano's Mask vs. Mask match with Chad Gable's Americano in May, this match was excellent in its own right.

Americano survived the shenanigans and emerged the new AAA Mega champion, much to the delight of the audience in attendance. AAA has nailed the presentation of Americano this year and has turned what should have been a career killer of a gimmick into an undeniable attraction for AAA.

The former Ludwig Kaiser will unfortunately still have a ceiling when he inevitably returns to the main roster, but for now, he's the perfect person to build the brand around. He's the biggest babyface in the promotion after seeing his story culminate on the grand stage.

AAA doing right by Americano should instill confidence in fans that AAA can be a place be where WWE's most underutilized athletes and miscast competitors such as Americano, Omos and others get their second chance at a career resurgence.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: The 6 Top NHL Dramas From Summer 2026
articles.summary: The Summer of 2026 could be considered among the most consequential in recent NHL history.
articles.body:
The Summer of 2026 could be considered among the most consequential in recent NHL history.

An "Original Six" team made numerous changes in the hope of returning to playoff contender status.

Two stars' trade requests become public knowledge, sparking weeks of speculation about their potential destinations. One of them resulted in a team's long search for a new general manager.

Meanwhile, a controversial coach received another opportunity to resume his NHL career. A blockbuster trade reunited two brothers, and an offer sheet had far-reaching consequences for teams attempting to re-sign their best players.

Follow along as we examine these stories in what was a summer of drama for the NHL.

Toronto Maple Leafs Overhaul Their Roster

After nine straight appearances in the Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Toronto Maple Leafs missed the cut last season. It led to the firing of general manager Brad Treliving on March 30 , kicking off an offseason filled with drama in Leafs Nation.

Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment president Keith Pelley drew criticism for his handling of the issues that led to the club's downfall and his plans for the team.

The flak intensified when he hired former Arizona Coyotes general manager John Chayka as the Leafs' new GM. Chayka faced searing questions from the Toronto sports media during his introductory press conference about his tenure with the Coyotes, including the circumstances that led to his firing in 2020.

Despite his critics, Chayka wasted little time making changes in the front office, behind the bench, and within the roster. Among them was replacing Craig Berube as head coach with former Los Angeles Kings bench boss Jim Hiller.

Chayka's roster moves included acquiring starting goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky, first-pairing defenseman Darren Raddysh, and forwards Nick Paul, Jack Roslovic, Colton Sissons, Teddy Blueger, and Brandon Duhaime.

The most notable addition was winger Gavin McKenna. Chosen first overall after the Maple Leafs won the 2026 draft lottery, providing Leafs fans with a ray of hope following a miserable season. NHL Central Scouting ranked the 18-year-old as the top prospect in the 2026 draft class.

On paper, the Maple Leafs seem better than last year's bunch. Whether they'll be good enough to return to playoff contention remains to be seen. Nevertheless, the early offseason turmoil in the league's biggest market drew plenty of attention among NHL followers.

Detroit Red Wings Search For a New General Manager

On July 15, the Detroit Red Wings surprised the hockey world by announcing that Steve Yzerman was no longer their general manager and executive vice president. He'd been GM since 2019 but failed to end a postseason drought that reached a decade by the end of last season.

Yzerman is a franchise icon for leading the Red Wings to three Stanley Cups during his 22-season Hall-of-Fame playing career. As Tampa Bay Lightning GM, he'd built the foundation of the roster that became Cup champions in 2020 and 2021. However, he couldn't replicate that success as the Wings GM.

Dylan Larkin's trade request , which became public in early June, was the last straw. After 11 seasons with the Red Wings, the last six as team captain, the 30-year-old center apparently grew weary of the constant losing. He'd also clashed with Yzerman .

Two weeks after Yzerman was relieved of his duties, the Red Wings announced they'd hired a search firm to find a suitable replacement. The intention was to find an analytics-driven general manager.

As the calendar flipped to September, however, the Wings haven't found a new GM. With training camp fast approaching and the regular season less than three weeks away, NHL insiders claimed that several potential candidates hadn't even been interviewed yet.

While questions arose about the search process, others wondered if the new general manager would have sufficient time to mend fences with Larkin or find a suitable trade partner among his limited list of trade destinations.

Meanwhile, restricted free agent defenseman Simon Edvinsson remains unsigned. He said he'll remain patient and is returning to Detroit for training camp . However, he can't participate unless he's under contract, adding further intrigue to an already puzzling drama.

Mike Babcock Becomes the Edmonton Oilers' New Head Coach

On June 23, the Edmonton Oilers named Mike Babcock as their new head coach , replacing Kris Knoblauch, who had guided them to the Stanley Cup Final in 2024 and 2025.

Babcock's hiring was rumored for weeks. However, the move still raised eyebrows around the league given his controversial history since 2019.

Before that year, Babcock was considered among the NHL's most respected and successful head coaches. He'd guided the Anaheim Ducks to the Stanley Cup Final in 2003, the Detroit Red Wings to a Stanley Cup championship, and coached Canada to Olympic gold in 2010 and 2014.

Hired by the Toronto Maple Leafs in 2015, Babcock quickly turned their rebuilding roster into a perennial playoff team. However, he was replaced by Sheldon Keefe in November 2019 following a poor start to the season.

Soon after Babcock's firing, he was accused of bullying and mistreating players , going back to his days with the Ducks. Hired by the Columbus Blue Jackets on July 1, 2023, he stepped down before training camp that fall following accusations that he improperly viewed players' smartphones.

Babcock was cleared to return to coaching following a league review. Oilers stars Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl, and Zach Hyman also endorsed him , with Hyman crediting the embattled coach for helping his development during his tenure with the Maple Leafs.

Nevertheless, Babcock's hiring received mixed reactions on social media. Some believe the Oilers could benefit from being held accountable by an old-school, hard-nosed coach, while others doubt this story will end well. If so, the drama may be just getting started in Edmonton.

Trades That Could Happen Before Training Camp

Brady Tkachuk Traded to the Florida Panthers

Several notable trades took place during the summer of 2026 . The Washington Capitals acquired wingers Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou. The Chicago Blackhawks brought in Bowen Byram. The San Jose Sharks traded for Darnell Nurse, and the Utah Mammoth traded for Vincent Trocheck.

However, the biggest and most dramatic move occurred on June 21, when the Florida Panthers acquired winger and team captain Brady Tkachuk from the Ottawa Senators in exchange for two first-round picks in the 2026 draft, a second-rounder in 2027, and a conditional first-rounder in 2029.

It had long been rumored that Tkachuk wanted to join the Panthers and play alongside his older brother, Matthew. Brady spent the past two years denying the conjecture , claiming he was fully committed to the Senators and the city of Ottawa.

Senators general manager Steve Staios also denied the rumors . Following the Tkachuk trade, however, he admitted the 26-year-old winger requested a trade 10 days after their season ended on Apr. 25, when the Carolina Hurricanes swept them in the first round of the playoffs.

Tkachuk said he requested the trade to start the next chapter of his career. He thanked the Senators and the city of Ottawa for supporting and believing in him, but felt he had a better chance of winning with the Panthers.

Since the trade, the Senators' players have claimed they've put it behind them and are moving on. Staios wasted little time attempting to replace his former captain's scoring, acquiring wingers William Eklund and Andre Burakovsky.

However, the trade left some Senators fans feeling betrayed . That could make for an interesting situation when Tkachuk returns to Ottawa to face his former team on Oct. 21.

Trade Requests by Dylan Larkin and Connor Hellebuyck

An NHL player's trade request rarely becomes public knowledge. In most cases, they aren't revealed until after the move takes place, as when the Ottawa Senators shipped Brady Tkachuk to the Florida Panthers on June 21.

However, the summer of 2026 saw two notable stars' trade requests become common knowledge, sparking speculation among fans and pundits about the reasons and the potential destinations.

On June 5, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin had requested a trade. Nearly three months later, on Aug. 27, Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck revealed that he also asked to be traded.

Larkin, 30, has spent his entire 11-season NHL career with the Red Wings, the last five as team captain. He didn't reveal the reason behind his request, but it's believed he's frustrated over the club's decade-long playoff drought and tensions with GM Steve Yzerman, who was relieved of his duties in mid-July.

Hellebuyck is the only active three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also won the Hart Memorial Trophy in 2024-25 and backstopped Team USA to Olympic gold in men's hockey in February. In a statement, he felt it was best for he and his family to move on to a team where he can win the Stanley Cup.

Larkin and Hellebuyck are attempting to pressure their respective teams into moving them quickly. Some observers considered their trade requests examples of growing player empowerment as they seek to assert more control over their careers.

However, Larkin remains with the Red Wings as they search for a new general manager, indicating he'll report to their training camp this week. Meanwhile, Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff has a history of patiently waiting for the right deal, which could force Hellebuyck to stick around longer than expected .

On July 3, the Philadelphia Flyers stunned the NHL world by signing Anaheim Ducks restricted free agent center Leo Carlsson to a five-year offer sheet worth a league-record average annual value of $18 million.

Offer sheets were once a rarely used tactic by NHL general managers to try to sign away another team's restricted free agents. Because they're usually matched, they're often considered a waste of time. Another deterrent is the expensive compensation rate owed to the losing team.

In recent years, however, a few teams have had some success . In August 2021, the Carolina Hurricanes signed away center Jesperi Kotkaniemi from the Montreal Canadiens. Three years later, the St. Louis Blues signed winger Dylan Holloway and defenseman Philip Broberg from the Edmonton Oilers.

The Carlsson offer sheet, however, was significant because of how much the promising 21-year-old center received. For several days, fans and reporters mulled over what the Ducks would do before they ended the suspense by matching the offer on July 9 .

It was a bold attempt by the Flyers to address their need for a first-line center. By matching the offer, the Ducks found themselves with limited salary-cap space and rising star Cutter Gauthier to re-sign. To address that issue, they terminated winger Chris Kreider's contract.

The Carlsson offer sheet was possible because of the dramatic increase in the NHL salary cap from $95.5 million to $104 million. It kicked off a rapid rise in salaries for star players regardless of where they are in their respective careers.

Carlsson's league-leading AAV was swiftly replaced by rising star Macklin Celebrini's $18.8 million AAV on a five-year extension with the San Jose Sharks. Colorado Avalanche superstar Cale Makar broke that record a month later with a $20.4 million AAV on an eight-year deal.

It also prompted some teams to avoid future offer-sheet risks by signing their promising youngsters to lucrative deals at previously unheard-of amounts. The most notable example was the eight-year extension worth $9.38 million AAV signed by Vancouver Canucks defenseman Zeev Buium on Sep. 4.

Stats and standings via NHL.com . Salary cap and contract info via PuckPedia .

articles.title: South Korea’s new manager Robert Moreno dismisses ‘AI coaching’ allegations
articles.summary: The Spanish manager has been appointed South Korea’s interim head coach following a disastrous World Cup campaign.
articles.body:
South Korea’s new interim football coach Robert Moreno has denied allegations that he relied on artificial intelligence during his last coaching role but admitted to using technology in his work.

Addressing his first news conference as the Taegeuk Warriors’ temporary coach on Monday, Moreno promised to make South Korean football fans “happy”.

The Spaniard was appointed as the Asian giants’ temporary coach following a disastrous few months for the team and the country’s football federation, during which on-field results and off-field controversies left the fans bitterly disappointed.

Moreno, who was forced to deny earlier this year that he used ChatGPT to prepare for games, will be in charge for friendly matches in the coming months.

He addressed allegations that he used artificial intelligence during his time in charge of Russian club Sochi, saying “It was a piece of news that is completely false and went viral.”

Moreno left the top-flight side in September 2025 after a poor run of results, and reports said he had heavily relied on ChatGPT in his role, even using it to decide between potential signings.

“Anyone who spends 10 minutes looking into it can see that everything has been taken out of context and put together to cause harm.”

The Korea Football Association (KFA) said Moreno could stay on for the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January-February, “subject to an evaluation”.

Moreno named captain Son Heung-min in his squad for four upcoming home friendlies and said he wanted to put a smile back on South Korean fans’ faces.

“We’re going to try to do our work honestly and with the aim of making all Korean football fans happy,” said the 48-year-old, who is the first Spaniard to coach South Korea.

“Good matches, and trying to help the players.”

Moreno will lead the team against Ecuador and Uruguay in September and Venezuela and Uzbekistan in October.

South Korea had been without a coach since Hong Myung-bo quit following their shock group-stage exit from the World Cup in North America in June.

Hong’s departure did little to quell public outrage over the disappointing campaign and added fuel to pre-existing questions about how he was hired.

Police raided KFA headquarters last month as part of an investigation into Hong’s 2024 appointment.

The KFA also apologised for allegations that it provided sexual entertainment for foreign referees.

Moreno named striker Son, now in the United States’ Major League Soccer with Los Angeles FC, in his first squad along with Atletico Madrid’s Lee Kang-in and Bayern Munich’s Kim Min-jae.

Hong’s decision to leave Son on the bench in the first half of the decisive match against South Africa at the World Cup baffled and angered many supporters.

“We’re all aware of Son’s versatility,” said Moreno.

“For me, he can play in three positions.”

articles.title: Lakers predicted to sign $15M former first-rounder to revive career, learn from Luka Doncic
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers still have some roster moves to make. They have the opportunity to sign a recently released first round pick to help revitalize career...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have made a lot of offseason moves this summer as they hope to make some major playoff runs in the near future. It is time for Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves to lead the way for the organization.

The Lakers will bring in an almost entirely new look, which is fine. However, some believe that their team is still incomplete.

"I think there's plenty of time here before they have to make a decision. They do, I believe, still want to make some type of trade upgrade at the wing/forward spot after missing out on Jonathan Kuminga . I do think the Lakers are incomplete right now moving forward," Bleacher Report's Jake Fischer said.

LA has some room to make moves, but the problem is that they have been unsuccessful in moving guys off the roster. A roster move they could look to make is signing former first-round pick Cam Whitmore to a deal.

"Whitmore is far from a polished product and doesn't have the tools to shine defensively, at least not yet, but for someone who still has two-way eligibility, perhaps a team like L.A. could consider giving Whitmore a chance," Heavy.com's Adel Ahmad wrote.

Whitmore was traded in August to the Cleveland Cavaliers in the Peyton Watson deal. However, he was quickly waived by Cleveland.

"They get Cam Whitmore as part of the trade. They are going to waive and stretch Whitmore over three years. It's basically a $1.8 million cap hold that will then give them the flexibility to go out and sign James Harden to a new deal," ESPN's Bobby Marks said.

Whitmore is a wonderful scorer, and a team can never have too many of those. It is his defense that lacks productivity, but that is nothing a good coaching staff can't fix.

Whitmore was on his $15 million rookie deal before being waived. Whitmore would do a great job learning from Doncic and how he goes about his business. Doncic has also gotten better on the defensive side of the ball over the last year, so Whitmore can pick his brain on multiple things.

articles.title: Oilers’ Connor McDavid reveals why he is ‘a happy guy’ despite NHL pressure
articles.summary: Connor McDavid talks about family and gratitude.
articles.body:
Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid says the pressure of NHL hockey has not taken away his enjoyment of life. McDavid opened up about finding joy while speaking with Sportsnet's Kyle Bukauskas and Elliotte Friedman.

Bukauskas asked McDavid whether he could "find joy" during a demanding NHL season. The Oilers captain offered a clear answer.

"I am a happy guy," McDavid said. "I live a great life. I have a great wife and a great family, and my life is absolutely great."

McDavid has been married to interior designer Lauren Kyle since July 2024. The wedding took place in Muskoka, Ontario, years after the couple initially started dating in 2015. They currently live in a custom Edmonton home with their miniature Bernedoodle, Lenny, and enjoy strong support from McDavid's parents and brother.

McDavid also explained why hockey pressure feels different from an ordinary burden. "I'm extremely grateful for how my life is, and I feel incredibly grateful that I am so passionate about what I do," he said.

"There are a lot of people in the world that don't get to live with that passion, what they do every day. And so I feel very lucky that I get to do what I do and live the life that I live, and I'm very happy to be doing that."

That mindset matters as Edmonton enters another season with significant expectations. McDavid remains central to the Oilers' championship hopes after another elite individual campaign.

Connor McDavid 's mindset meets Oilers' championship pressure

Edmonton Oilers center Connor McDavid (97) warms up at SAP Center. Mandatory Credit: David Gonzales-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The Oilers are coming off a difficult 2025-26 season that ended with a first-round playoff loss. Edmonton finished 41-30-11, then lost to Anaheim in six games.

McDavid still produced at an elite level, leading the NHL with 138 points. However, Edmonton allowed 265 goals, ranking 25th league-wide, exposing structural problems beyond its captain.

The organization responded with major changes across the roster and coaching staff. Mike Babcock replaced Kris Knoblauch, while Edmonton also revamped its defense and goaltending options.

McDavid's attitude provides value, but that is not going to mask Edmonton's structural issues. The Oilers need better defensive support and reliable goaltending around their star to reach the 2024 Stanley Cup Final level.

"We come a shot away from the ultimate goal," McDavid said about the Game 7 loss in 2024. "Come a couple of games away [in 2025], then the following year, you almost take it for granted that you're this team that's just going to figure it out and be there. But that's not how it works at all."

A focused mindset could prove important during another high-pressure season. Edmonton's championship window remains tied closely to McDavid, but the roster must improve around him.

The Oilers begin their 2026-27 campaign against the Vancouver Canucks on Tuesday, Sept. 29, with expectations again centered on a deep playoff run.
